    README:
    🎬 YouTube AI Agent > Fully automated AI pipeline that researches, scripts, voices, edits, and uploads a 30-day YouTube video series — from a single command. Built with CrewAI, Groq (LLaMA 3.3 70B), Kokoro TTS, Pexels, MoviePy, and the YouTube Data API v3. 100% free APIs. 100% open-source. --- Table of Contents - What It Does - How the AI Agent Works - Tech Stack - Project Structure - Windows Setup — Step by Step - macOS / Linux Setup - Configuration - YouTube API Setup - How to Run - GitHub Actions — Automated Daily Upload - Troubleshooting - Roadmap --- What It Does Give the agent a topic — e.g. "Personal Finance for Beginners" — and it autonomously: 1. Researches trending subtopics and viewer questions on the web 2. Plans a 30-day content calendar with unique daily angles 3. Writes scripts for YouTube Shorts (55–58 s) or long-form faceless videos (7–8 min) 4. Downloads matching royalty-free stock footage from Pexels 5. Generates a professional voiceover using Kokoro TTS (runs locally — no API cost) 6. Assembles the final video — clips + voiceover + background music + text overlays 7. Uploads to YouTube with SEO-optimised title, description, and tags — scheduled 24 h apart --- How the AI Agent Works The pipeline uses a multi-agent architecture built on CrewAI. Each agent has a focused role, backstory, and tools. Agents run sequentially — each output feeds the next. ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ YouTubePipeline │ │ │ │ Phase 1 — Planning │ │ ┌──────────────────┐ │ │ │ Research Agent │ ← Tavily Web Search │ │ │ (Strategist) │ Outputs: 30-day JSON calendar │ │ └────────┬─────────┘ │ │ │ │ │ Phase 2 — Production (per video) │ │ │ │ │ ┌────────▼─────────┐ │ │ │ Script Agent │ ← Groq / LLaMA 3.3 70B │ │ │ (Writer) │ Outputs: hook + body + CTA JSON │ │ └────────┬─────────┘ │ │ ┌────────▼─────────┐ │ │ │ Media Agent │ ← Pexels API │ │ │ (Director) │ Outputs: 4-6 downloaded .mp4 clips │ │ └────────┬─────────┘ │ │ ┌────────▼─────────┐ │ │ │ Voice Agent │ ← Kokoro TTS (local) │ │ │ (Narrator) │ Outputs: voiceover .wav │ │ └────────┬─────────┘ │ │ ┌────────▼─────────┐ │ │ │ Editor Agent │ ← MoviePy │ │ │ (Post-Prod.) │ Outputs: final .mp4 at correct res │ │ └────────┬─────────┘ │ │ │ │ │ Phase 3 — Publishing │ │ │ │ │ ┌────────▼─────────┐ │ │ │ Publisher Agent │ ← YouTube Data API v3 │ │ │ (SEO + Upload) │ Outputs: YouTube video ID + URL │ │ └──────────────────┘ │ └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ Agent Breakdown | Agent | Role | Tools | Output | |---|---|---|---| | Research Agent | Content Strategist | Tavily Search | 30-day JSON calendar | | Script Agent | Scriptwriter | LLM (Groq) | Script JSON with hook, body, CTA | | Media Agent | Visual Director | Pexels API | Downloaded .mp4 clips | | Voice Agent | Narrator | Kokoro TTS | .wav voiceover file | | Editor Agent | Post-Production | MoviePy | Final .mp4 video | | Publisher Agent | SEO & Distribution | YouTube API | Video URL | --- Tech Stack | Layer | Tool | Free Tier | |---|---|---| | Agent Orchestration | CrewAI | Open-source | | LLM | Groq — LLaMA 3.3 70B | 14,400 req/day | | Web Research | Tavily Search API | 1,000 searches/month | | Text-to-Speech | Kokoro TTS | Fully local/free | | Stock Footage | Pexels API | 200 req/hour | | Video Assembly | MoviePy | Open-source | | YouTube Upload | YouTube Data API v3 | 10,000 units/day | | Package Manager | uv | Open-source | | State / DB | TinyDB | Open-source | | CLI | Click + Rich | Open-source | Total infrastructure cost: $0 --- Project Structure yt-agent/ │ ├── youtubeaiagent/ ← Main package │ ├── agents/init.py ← All 6 CrewAI agent definitions │ ├── tasks/videotasks.py ← Task definitions per pipeline stage │ ├── tools/ │ │ ├── tavilytool.py ← Web research │ │ ├── pexelstool.py ← Stock video/image downloader │ │ ├── ttstool.py ← Kokoro TTS + gTTS fallback │ │ ├── editortool.py ← MoviePy video assembly │ │ └── youtubetool.py ← YouTube OAuth + upload │ ├── pipeline/ │ │ ├── crew.py ← Core orchestrator │ │ ├── scheduler.py ← Batch and daily server modes │ │ └── state.py ← TinyDB job tracker │ └── config/ │ ├── settings.py ← Pydantic settings │ └── prompts.py ← All LLM prompt templates │ ├── tests/testpipeline.py ├── output/ ← Generated content (gitignored) │ └── music/ ← Drop .mp3 files here for background music ├── config/ ├── .github/workflows/ ← GitHub Actions automation ├── main.py ← CLI entry point ├── setupyoutubeauth.py ← One-time YouTube OAuth helper ├── install.bat ← Windows one-click installer ├── install.sh ← macOS / Linux installer ├── requirements.txt └── .env.example --- Windows Setup — Step by Step > Why uv? Previous versions of this guide used pip, which caused a chain of errors > (pkgresources, pydanticcore, cygrpc, onnxruntime, numpy) because pip installs > packages one at a time and they overwrite each other's compiled extensions. > uv resolves the entire dependency graph in one shot — none of those errors can occur. --- Step 1 — Install Python 3.11 Download from python.org/downloads and run the installer. > ⚠️ During install, tick "Add Python to PATH" — this is unchecked by default. > Choose the Windows installer (64-bit) version. Verify in a new terminal: cmd python --version Should print Python 3.11.x or higher. --- Step 2 — Install ffmpeg ffmpeg is required for video rendering. 1. Download from ffmpeg.org/download.html → Windows builds → download a release zip 2. Extract it to C:\ffmpeg 3. Add C:\ffmpeg\bin to your Windows PATH: - Search Windows → "Edit the system environment variables" - Click Environment Variables - Under System variables, select Path → Edit → New - Add C:\ffmpeg\bin - Click OK on all dialogs 4. Open a new terminal and verify: cmd ffmpeg -version --- Step 3 — Open Command Prompt in the project folder cmd cd E:\Projects\AI\youtube-ai-agent\yt-agent > Use Command Prompt (cmd). If you use PowerShell, first run: > Set-ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned -Scope CurrentUser --- Step 4 — Install uv Open PowerShell (not cmd) and run: powershell powershell -c "irm | iex" Close PowerShell. Open a new Command Prompt and verify: cmd uv --version > uv is a modern Python package manager that resolves the full dependency graph in one > pass. It prevents every compiled-extension error that pip causes on Windows. --- Step 5 — Create a fresh virtual environment Back in Command Prompt inside the project folder: cmd uv venv venv --python 3.11 --- Step 6 — Activate the virtual environment cmd venv\Scripts\activate You will see (venv) at the start of your prompt. Run this every time you open a new terminal to work on this project. --- Step 7 — Install PyTorch PyTorch must be installed first and separately because it uses a custom package index. cmd uv pip install torch==2.4.0 torchvision torchaudio --index-url This downloads 500 MB. It will take a few minutes. --- Step 8 — Install all dependencies cmd uv pip install -r requirements.txt uv resolves and installs the entire graph in one pass. No incremental errors. --- Step 9 — Install the project cmd uv pip install -e . This makes the youtubeaiagent package importable and prevents ModuleNotFoundError. --- Step 10 — Set up your API keys cmd copy .env.example .env Open .env in Notepad and fill in your three free API keys: env GROQAPIKEY=yourkeyhere TAVILYAPIKEY=yourkeyhere PEXELSAPIKEY=yourkeyhere Where to get them — all free, no credit card: | Key | Sign up at | Free limit | |---|---|---| | GROQAPIKEY | console.groq.com | 14,400 requests/day | | TAVILYAPIKEY | app.tavily.com | 1,000 searches/month | | PEXELSAPIKEY | pexels.com/api | 200 requests/hour | --- Step 11 — Verify the installation cmd python main.py --help You should see the CLI help menu. If that works, run your first real command: cmd python main.py plan --topic "Personal Finance for Beginners" This generates your 30-day content calendar. No video is produced and nothing is uploaded — safe to run as a first test. --- Step 12 — Set up YouTube uploads (one time only) Skip this until you are ready to actually upload videos. cmd python setupyoutubeauth.py See YouTube API Setup for how to get the required credentials. --- Every time you return to the project cmd cd E:\Projects\AI\youtube-ai-agent\yt-agent venv\Scripts\activate python main.py --help --- One-click installer (alternative to Steps 4–9) If you prefer, just double-click install.bat after completing Steps 1–3. It runs Steps 4–9 automatically and ends by running python main.py --help to confirm success. --- macOS / Linux Setup Step 1 — Install system dependencies bash macOS brew install python@3.11 ffmpeg Ubuntu / Debian sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y python3.11 python3.11-venv ffmpeg Step 2 — Install uv bash curl -LsSf | sh source $HOME/.local/bin/env # or restart terminal uv --version Step 3 — Clone and set up bash cd /path/to/yt-agent uv venv venv --python 3.11 source venv/bin/activate uv pip install torch==2.4.0 torchvision torchaudio \ --index-url uv pip install -r requirements.txt uv pip install -e . Step 4 — Configure and test bash cp .env.example .env Edit .env and add your API keys python main.py --help python main.py plan --topic "Personal Finance for Beginners" --- Configuration All settings live in .env. Copy .env.example to get started. env ── Required ────────────────────────────────────────────────── GROQAPIKEY=gskxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx TAVILYAPIKEY=tvly-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx PEXELSAPIKEY=xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx ── Optional (defaults shown) ───────────────────────────────── GROQMODEL=llama-3.3-70b-versatile KOKOROVOICE=afheart # afheart | afbella | amadam KOKOROSPEED=1.1 SHORTSDURATIONSECONDS=58 LONGVIDEODURATIONSECONDS=480 MUSICVOLUME=0.15 LOGLEVEL=INFO Add background music (optional) Drop any royalty-free .mp3 or .wav files into output/music/. The editor picks one at random for each video. Free source: Free Music Archive --- YouTube API Setup One-time setup to let the agent upload to your YouTube channel. Step 1 — Enable the API 1. Go to console.cloud.google.com 2. Create a new project — e.g. youtube-ai-agent 3. APIs & Services → Library → YouTube Data API v3 → Enable Step 2 — Create OAuth credentials 1. APIs & Services → Credentials → Create Credentials → OAuth 2.0 Client ID 2. Application type: Desktop App 3. Download the JSON file 4. Save it as config/clientsecrets.json inside your project folder Step 3 — Authorise cmd python setupyoutubeauth.py A browser window opens. Sign in with the Google account that owns your YouTube channel. Credentials are saved to config/youtubecredentials.json and auto-refresh going forward. --- How to Run Preview 30-day content plan (no video produced) cmd python main.py plan --topic "Personal Finance for Beginners" Force regenerate even if cached python main.py plan --topic "Personal Finance for Beginners" --force Single test video — Shorts cmd python main.py run --topic "Personal Finance for Beginners" --format short --days 1 Single test video — no upload (dry run) cmd python main.py run --topic "Personal Finance for Beginners" --format short --days 1 --no-upload Full 30-day Shorts series with scheduled uploads cmd python main.py run --topic "Personal Finance for Beginners" --format short --days 30 --schedule "2024-12-01T09:00:00" Both Shorts and long-form cmd python main.py run --topic "Personal Finance for Beginners" --format both --days 30 --schedule "2024-12-01T09:00:00" Resume from a specific day cmd python main.py run --topic "Personal Finance for Beginners" --format short --days 19 --start-day 12 Check pipeline status cmd python main.py status --topic "Personal Finance for Beginners" Run tests cmd pytest tests/ -v --- GitHub Actions — Automated Daily Upload Setup 1. Push this repo to GitHub 2. Add the following secrets under Settings → Secrets and Variables → Actions: | Secret | Value | |---|---| | GROQAPIKEY | Your Groq key | | TAVILYAPIKEY | Your Tavily key | | PEXELSAPIKEY | Your Pexels key | | YOUTUBECLIENTSECRETS | Full contents of config/clientsecrets.json | | YOUTUBECREDENTIALS | Full contents of config/youtubecredentials.json | 3. The workflow runs daily at 6 PM UTC, produces one video, and uploads it. 4. Trigger manually from the Actions tab with any topic and format. --- Troubleshooting ❌ No module named 'pkgresources' crewai 0.x imports pkgresources in its telemetry module. Run the included patch script which replaces it with Python's built-in importlib.metadata: cmd python patchcrewai.py python main.py --help --- ❌ Any other compiled extension error (pydanticcore, cygrpc, onnxruntime, numpy) All of these have the same root cause — pip installed a package for the wrong Python version or corrupted the environment mid-install. The fix is always the same: nuke the venv and reinstall with uv. cmd cd E:\Projects\AI\youtube-ai-agent\yt-agent REM Delete the broken venv rmdir /s /q venv REM Recreate with uv uv venv venv --python 3.11 venv\Scripts\activate uv pip install torch==2.4.0 torchvision torchaudio --index-url uv pip install -r requirements.txt uv pip install -e . python patchcrewai.py python main.py --help --- ❌ uv: command not found Install uv first (Step 4 above): powershell powershell -c "irm | iex" Then open a new terminal. --- ❌ python: command not found or wrong version Reinstall Python 3.11 from python.org, tick "Add Python to PATH", pick 64-bit. --- ❌ ffmpeg: command not found Install ffmpeg and add C:\ffmpeg\bin to your Windows PATH. See Step 2 above. --- ❌ ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'youtubeaiagent' cmd uv pip install -e . --- ❌ ValidationError on startup Your .env file is missing or API keys are not filled in. cmd copy .env.example .env REM Then open .env and add your keys --- ❌ venv\Scripts\activate fails in PowerShell powershell Set-ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned -Scope CurrentUser --- ❌ YouTube HttpError 403 quotaExceeded 10,000 units/day free. Each upload costs 1,600 units (6 uploads/day max). Use --schedule to spread uploads or request a free quota increase from Google Cloud Console. --- ❌ YouTube HttpError 401 Invalid Credentials cmd del config\youtubecredentials.json python setupyoutubeauth.py --- Quick error reference | Error | Fix | |---|---| | pkgresources, pydanticcore, cygrpc, onnxruntime, numpy errors | Nuke venv and reinstall with uv (see above) | | uv: command not found | Run the uv install command in PowerShell | | python: command not found | Reinstall Python 3.11 64-bit, tick "Add to PATH" | | ffmpeg: command not found | Install ffmpeg, add C:\ffmpeg\bin to PATH | | ModuleNotFoundError: youtubeaiagent | uv pip install -e . | | ValidationError on startup | Fill in API keys in .env | | venv\Scripts\activate fails | Run Set-ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned in PowerShell | | YouTube 403 quotaExceeded | Use --schedule to spread uploads across days | | YouTube 401 Invalid Credentials | Delete credentials file and re-run setupyoutubeauth.py | --- Roadmap - [ ] Auto-generate thumbnails (Stable Diffusion / Pollinations.ai) - [ ] Burn auto-captions using Whisper timestamps - [ ] Background music auto-downloader (Free Music Archive API) - [ ] YouTube Analytics feedback loop — optimise future content based on views - [ ] Web dashboard (FastAPI + React) for pipeline monitoring --- License MIT — see LICENSE for details. --- Built for creators who want to automate content without sacrificing quality. ⭐ Star this repo if it helped | 🐛 Report an issue | 💡 Request a feature

    Description: This project is a fully‑automated pipeline that takes a topic string, generates a video script with GPT‑4o, converts the script to speech via Microsoft edge‑tts, builds a simple slideshow video with MoviePy, and uploads the resulting MP4 to YouTube through the YouTube Data API v3
    Language: Python

    README:
    YouTube Auto-Upload AI Agent 🚀 This project is a fully‑automated pipeline that takes a topic string, generates a video script with GPT‑4o, converts the script to speech via Microsoft edge‑tts, builds a simple slideshow video with MoviePy, and uploads the resulting MP4 to YouTube through the YouTube Data API v3. ✨ Features 1. Idea → YouTube in one command: python main.py "Your topic". 2. Saves the generated script as captions (in description). 3. Uses pure Python; no paid TTS keys needed—edge-tts relies on Microsoft voices. 4. Keeps uploads private by default so you can review before publishing. 5. Configuration via config.json (see configexample.json). 🛠️ Quick Start bash python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate # Optional virtualenv pip install -r requirements.txt Copy config and add keys cp configexample.json config.json nano config.json # Add your OPENAIAPIKEY etc. Place Google OAuth clientsecret.json in project root python main.py "Top 3 open‑source AI tools 2025" > First run will open a browser window asking you to authorize the YouTube upload scope. A token.json is cached for future runs. 📁 Project structure youtubeaiagent/ ├── main.py ├── requirements.txt ├── README.md └── configexample.json 📝 Configuration (configexample.json) json { "openaiapikey": "sk-...", "voice": "en-US-GuyNeural", "video": { "slideduration": 5, "fps": 24, "resolution": [1280, 720] }, "youtube": { "privacystatus": "private", "categoryid": "27" } } 🧑‍💻 How it works 1. Script generation – GPT‑4 writes 250‑word script. 2. Sentence splitting – Regex splits into sentences (≈slides). 3. Slide rendering – Pillow draws white 1280×720 image with text. 4. Voice‑over – edge‑tts saves MP3 using desired voice. 5. Video assembly – MoviePy concatenatevideoclips + audio overlay. 6. Upload – Google API client uploads the file. 🔐 Quotas & Safety Upload costs 1 600 units of daily YouTube quota. Keep privacystatus private for manual review. Respect YouTube Community Guidelines; you are responsible for content. 🏗️ Next Steps Replace static slides with DALL·E or Pexels video b‑roll. Add subtitles track using youtube.captions().insert. Deploy on GitHub Actions nightly. --- ScreenShots Made with ❤️ by Khushal Singh

    README:
    🎬 VideoGenius AI - YouTube Video Generator SaaS Transform any topic into viral YouTube content with the power of AI 🚀 Live Demo • 📖 Documentation • 🛠️ Installation • 🤝 Contributing --- 🌟 Overview VideoGenius AI is a revolutionary SaaS platform that automates the entire YouTube video creation process. From script generation to final upload, our AI-powered system handles everything, enabling creators to scale from weekly uploads to daily content production effortlessly. ✨ Key Features - 🤖 AI Script Generation - GPT-4/GEMINI powered viral script creation - 🎨 Smart Visual Selection - Automatic stock footage and image selection - 🗣️ Professional Voiceover - Natural AI voice synthesis with 40+ voices - 🔄 Autopilot Mode - 24/7 automated video creation and scheduling - 📺 Direct YouTube Upload - Seamless channel integration with OAuth 2.0 - 📊 Advanced Analytics - Real-time performance tracking and insights - 🎯 SEO Optimization - AI-generated titles, descriptions, and tags 🏗️ Architecture Tech Stack Backend: - 🐘 Laravel 12 - Modern PHP framework with elegant syntax - 🔄 Inertia.js - SPA experience without API complexity - 🐳 Docker Compose - Containerized microservices architecture - 🗄️ MySQL 8.0 - Robust relational database - ⚡ Redis - High-performance caching and session storage - 🔧 n8n - Workflow automation and AI orchestration Frontend: - 💚 Vue.js 3 - Progressive JavaScript framework - 🎨 Tailwind CSS - Utility-first CSS framework - ✨ Custom Animations - Glassmorphism and particle effects - 📱 Responsive Design - Mobile-first approach - ⚡ Vite - Lightning-fast build tool AI & APIs: - 🧠 OpenAI GPT-4 or Gemini - Advanced script generation - 🎤 Text-to-Speech - Multiple TTS providers - 📸 Pexels API - High-quality stock media - 📺 YouTube API v3 - Direct channel integration - 🔐 Google OAuth 2.0 - Secure authentication System Architecture ┌─────────────────┐ ┌─────────────────┐ ┌─────────────────┐ │ Frontend │ │ Backend │ │ AI Services │ │ (Vue.js) │◄──►│ (Laravel) │◄──►│ (GPT-4, TTS) │ └─────────────────┘ └─────────────────┘ └─────────────────┘ │ │ │ ▼ ▼ ▼ ┌─────────────────┐ ┌─────────────────┐ ┌─────────────────┐ │ Web Server │ │ Database │ │ Media APIs │ │ (Nginx) │ │ (MySQL) │ │ (Pexels) │ └─────────────────┘ └─────────────────┘ └─────────────────┘ │ │ │ └───────────────────────┼───────────────────────┘ ▼ ┌─────────────────┐ │ Docker │ │ Compose │ └─────────────────┘ 🔧 n8n Workflow Integration VideoGenius AI leverages n8n as the core automation engine that orchestrates the entire video creation pipeline. The workflow handles AI service coordination, media processing, and YouTube publishing in a visual, node-based environment. 📋 Workflow Import The complete video generation workflow is defined in completevideogenerator.json. This workflow must be imported into your n8n instance to enable automated video creation. To import the workflow: 1. Access n8n Dashboard 2. Import Workflow - Click "Import from File" - Select workflows/completevideogenerator.json - The workflow will automatically connect to Laravel backend 3. Workflow Configuration bash No API credentials needed in n8n! Laravel handles all external API integrations: - OpenAI/GEMINI API (configured in Laravel .env) - Pexels API (configured in Laravel .env) - Google Cloud TTS (configured in Laravel .env) - YouTube API (OAuth handled by Laravel) # n8n only needs Laravel webhook endpoints 🏗️ n8n Workflow Architecture ┌─────────────────┐ ┌─────────────────┐ ┌─────────────────┐ │ Trigger │ │ Script Gen │ │ Media Search │ │ (Webhook) │───►│ (OpenAI) │───►│ (Pexels API) │ └─────────────────┘ └─────────────────┘ └─────────────────┘ │ │ ▼ ▼ ┌─────────────────┐ ┌─────────────────┐ ┌─────────────────┐ │ Status Update │ │ Voice Gen │ │ Media Filter │ │ (Laravel API) │◄───│ (TTS API) │◄───│ (Processing) │ └─────────────────┘ └─────────────────┘ └─────────────────┘ │ │ │ ▼ ▼ ▼ ┌─────────────────┐ ┌─────────────────┐ ┌─────────────────┐ │ Video Compile │ │ SEO Optimize │ │ YouTube Upload│ │ (Python Script)│───►│ (AI Generated)│───►│ (API v3) │ └─────────────────┘ └─────────────────┘ └─────────────────┘ │ │ │ └───────────────────────┼───────────────────────┘ ▼ ┌─────────────────┐ │ Final Status │ │ (Webhook) │ └─────────────────┘ 🎬 Workflow Nodes Breakdown 1. Webhook Trigger - Receives video creation requests from Laravel - Validates input parameters (topic, style, duration) - Initiates the automation pipeline 2. Script Generation (Laravel API Call) - Sends request to Laravel backend for script creation - Laravel handles OpenAI GPT-4 integration internally - Returns structured script with timestamps 3. Media Selection (Laravel API Call) - Requests media assets from Laravel backend - Laravel handles Pexels API integration and filtering - Returns curated media URLs and metadata 4. Voiceover Generation (Laravel API Call) - Sends script to Laravel for TTS processing - Laravel manages TTS service integration - Returns audio file URL and duration 5. Video Compilation (Laravel Queue Job) - Triggers Laravel queue job for video assembly - Laravel executes Python scripts internally - Combines all assets into final MP4 6. SEO Optimization (Laravel AI Service) - Requests optimized metadata from Laravel - Laravel generates title, description, and tags - Returns SEO-optimized content 7. YouTube Upload (Laravel OAuth) - Triggers Laravel YouTube upload service - Laravel handles OAuth authentication and API calls - Returns upload status and video URL 8. Status Updates (Laravel Webhooks) - Receives progress updates from Laravel - Updates workflow execution status - Triggers completion notifications ⚙️ Workflow Configuration Webhook URLs LARAVELAPPURL= N8NWEBHOOKURL= External API Endpoints GEMINIENDPOINT= PEXELSENDPOINT= YOUTUBEENDPOINT= 📊 Workflow Monitoring Monitor your n8n workflows through: - Execution History: Track success/failure rates - Performance Metrics: Average processing times - Error Logs: Debug failed executions - Resource Usage: CPU and memory consumption 🔄 Workflow Customization The completevideogenerator.json workflow can be customized for: - Different Content Types: Educational, entertainment, news - Brand Guidelines: Add custom intro/outro sequences - Publishing Schedules: Set automated upload timing - Quality Settings: Adjust video resolution and bitrate Advanced Customization: javascript // Example: Custom script generation prompt { "prompt": "Create a {{$json.style}} YouTube script about {{$json.topic}} that is {{$json.duration}} long, includes viral hooks, and targets {{$json.audience}} audience.", "maxtokens": 1500, "temperature": 0.7 } 🚀 Installation Prerequisites - Docker and Docker Compose - Git - Google Developer Account (for YouTube API) - OpenAI API Key Quick Start 1. Clone the repository bash git clone cd youtubeVideoGenerator 2. Environment Configuration bash cp .env.example .env 3. Configure your environment variables env Database DBCONNECTION=mysql DBHOST=db DBPORT=3306 DBDATABASE=youtubegenerator DBUSERNAME=root DBPASSWORD=secret Google OAuth & YouTube API GOOGLECLIENTID=yourgoogleclientid GOOGLECLIENTSECRET=yourgoogleclientsecret GOOGLEREDIRECTURI= AI Services OPENAIAPIKEY=youropenaiapikey PEXELSAPIKEY=yourpexelsapikey TTS Configuration TTSSERVICE=gTTS TTSLANGUAGE=en 4. Build and start the application bash docker-compose up -d --build 5. Install dependencies and setup bash Install PHP dependencies docker-compose exec app composer install Install Node.js dependencies docker-compose exec app npm install --legacy-peer-deps Generate application key docker-compose exec app php artisan key:generate Run database migrations docker-compose exec app php artisan migrate Build frontend assets docker-compose exec app npm run build 6. Access the application - Frontend: - n8n Workflow: - Database: localhost:3306 📁 Project Structure youtubeVideoGenerator/ ├── app/ │ ├── Http/Controllers/ # Application controllers │ ├── Models/ # Eloquent models │ ├── Services/ # Business logic services │ └── Jobs/ # Queue jobs for video processing ├── resources/ │ ├── js/ │ │ ├── Pages/ # Vue.js pages │ │ ├── Components/ # Reusable Vue components │ │ └── Layouts/ # Application layouts │ └── css/ # Stylesheets with animations ├── scripts/ │ ├── videogenerator.py # Python video assembly │ ├── ttsgenerator.py # Text-to-speech generation │ └── requirements.txt # Python dependencies ├── workflows/ │ └── completevideogenerator.json # n8n workflow (REQUIRED IMPORT) ├── docker-compose.yml # Container orchestration ├── Dockerfile # Application container └── README.md # This file 🚨 Important: n8n Workflow Setup The completevideogenerator.json file contains the core automation logic and MUST be imported into your n8n instance for the platform to function properly. 🎯 Usage Basic Workflow 1. Sign in with Google - Connect your YouTube channel 2. Create a Video - Provide a topic or keyword 3. AI Processing - Watch as AI generates script, selects visuals, and creates voiceover 4. Review & Edit - Make any necessary adjustments 5. Publish - Upload directly to your YouTube channel Autopilot Mode 1. Configure Channel Settings - Set your niche and preferences 2. Enable Autopilot - Choose your publishing schedule 3. Relax - AI creates and publishes videos automatically Advanced Features - Bulk Video Creation - Generate multiple videos from a list of topics - Custom Voice Selection - Choose from 40+ AI voices - Brand Customization - Add your logo and brand colors - Analytics Dashboard - Track performance across all videos 🔧 Configuration Google OAuth Setup 1.     README:
    PurffleShorts — Free AI YouTube Shorts Generator, Faceless Video Maker & Opus Clip Alternative English · 简体中文 · Español · Português · हिन्दी · 日本語 An open-source AI video generator for YouTube Shorts, TikTok and Instagram Reels. Give it a topic, a web page, a Reddit post or a long podcast, and it makes finished vertical videos (script, voiceover, footage, captions, sound effects), then uploads or schedules them on YouTube, TikTok and Instagram. YouTube automation in Python that runs on your own computer. The AI model you choose writes the script (GPT, Claude, Gemini, Llama through Ollama, DeepSeek, Grok, Mistral or any OpenAI-compatible API), using the phrases people actually search for on YouTube, and a second AI pass grades and rewrites it. Free neural voices read it, and stock footage, AI images or your own gameplay video fill the screen. Captions appear word by word, with key words in colour and an emoji per scene. It makes Reddit story videos, fake text message videos and two-voice dialogues, and clips podcasts into Shorts with jump cuts and face tracking. Free, MIT-licensed, no watermark. It also works from Claude Desktop, Claude Code and Cursor through MCP. Features · Quick start · Colab · Formats · Reddit & gameplay · Clip podcasts · SEO · AI models · Voices · Publishing · Studio · API · MCP · Compare · FAQ Real output, no editing: examples/flamingos.json , examples/dialogue.json and examples/chat-story.json rendered with make --script . Free Microsoft neural voices, AI images from Pollinations (for the octopus videos they were downloaded one by one into a local folder first, because keyless Pollinations now allows about one image every few minutes). GIFs have no sound. Try it with no API keys and no sign-up (needs uv): bash uvx --from git+ purffle-shorts demo --style chat …or open it in Google Colab and make videos in your browser, with nothing to install. ⭐ If PurffleShorts saves you time, a star helps other creators find it. · 🌐 purffle.com/purffle-shorts --- 🤖 What is PurffleShorts? PurffleShorts is a YouTube Shorts automation tool for faceless channels. Start it and it keeps going: fresh topic, retention-focused script that a second AI pass reviews and tightens, natural AI voiceover, relevant footage, captions synced to each spoken word, sound effects, a polished render, and an upload or scheduled release. It stays inside YouTube's daily API quota. Beyond the autopilot, it is a small studio: - Draft a script and edit any line before rendering. - Make two-voice dialogues, text-message stories and Reddit-style stories, over stock footage or your own gameplay background. - Turn an article or a Reddit post into a Short. - Clip a podcast into Shorts, an Opus Clip-style workflow that runs on your computer, with jump cuts, punch-in zoom and face tracking. - Publish the same video in several languages, and plan a week of ideas from what people search for on YouTube. - Let the channel's own view counts steer new scripts. It is made for content creators, faceless YouTube channels, educators and marketers who want short-form video at volume without editing by hand. It runs on your own computer (macOS, Windows, Linux), in Docker or in Google Colab. You pick every model, and the same video can go to TikTok and Instagram Reels as well as YouTube. --- 🎯 Use cases - A faceless channel on autopilot. Pick a niche (space, history, animals, money tips), set three publish times a day and leave it running. Ideas come from real YouTube searches, Trends, Wikipedia, Reddit, RSS or your list, and are never reused. The AI is told to avoid your recent titles, and every script is reviewed before it is voiced. - Reddit story videos over gameplay. The AI writes a first-person post, a narrator reads it over a post card, and your Minecraft parkour or other gameplay clip plays underneath: full screen, or split screen with footage on top. A real Reddit post link works as the source too. - Fake text message videos for Shorts, TikTok and Reels: the AI writes a fictional chat, two voices read it, and the phone screen is animated with a pop as each message lands. - Podcast, interview and stream clips. clip episode.mp4 --count 5 transcribes the video and lets the AI pick the moments that stand on their own (or the ones matching your brief, such as "the funniest bits"). You get captioned vertical clips with pauses and ums removed, the speaker kept in frame and a virality score each. There are no per-minute fees. - Articles, blog posts and notes into video. make --url or --from-file notes.md turns your own writing into a Short. - One idea, many languages. --also-lang es,hi,pt publishes the same video with native voices in each language. LOCALIZEMETADATA translates the title and description of every upload. - Education and explainers. Quiz, myth-vs-fact, explainer and dialogue formats, in 9:16 for Shorts or 16:9 for regular YouTube. - Automations and AI assistants. Drive it from n8n, Zapier or cron through the REST API, or ask Claude or Cursor to make, clip or upload videos through MCP. --- ✨ Features AI scriptwriting - One structured LLM call returns the whole Short: hook, scenes, a footage search, an image prompt, key words and an emoji per scene, title, description, hashtags, tags and YouTube category. - Script Doctor: a second AI pass grades the draft on six points (hook, curiosity, pacing, specificity, payoff, accuracy), lists what is weak and rewrites it. The rewrite is graded again and only kept if it scores at least as well, so the 0–100 retention score always belongs to the script you actually get. Automatic checks (hook length, filler words, missing call to action, no concrete numbers) feed the review. - Written for search: the phrases YouTube's own search box suggests for the topic are handed to the writer, so titles, descriptions and tags use the words people actually type. - Strict JSON-schema replies on providers that support them (OpenAI, Gemini, OpenRouter, Ollama, LM Studio, Claude), with an automatic step down for the ones that don't. - 12 providers: OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, Groq, OpenRouter, DeepSeek, Mistral, Together AI, xAI Grok, Ollama, LM Studio, or any OpenAI-compatible URL. List backups in LLMFALLBACKS and they are tried in order if the main one fails. - 11 formats: facts, story, listicle, myth-busting, quiz, explainer, motivational, news, two-voice dialogue, text-message story and Reddit-style story (a post card while the title is read, then the story with captions). - Draft first and edit any line in the Studio, or write a script yourself and render it with --script, with no LLM call. Sources - Your niches, questions people search for on YouTube (TOPICSOURCES=search), Google Trends, Wikipedia "On this day", Reddit TIL, RSS feeds, your own list, any web page or Reddit post (--url) or document (--from-file). - Content planner: the AI brainstorms a batch of specific, true, non-repeating ideas, guided by real YouTube searches, into a queue that the autopilot uses first. Voiceover - 320+ free Microsoft neural voices in 75 languages, with word-level timestamps. No key needed. - Two speakers for dialogues and chat stories, each with their own voice, joined with natural pauses. - One video, many languages: --also-lang es,hi adds translated copies that reuse the same footage. - Also OpenAI TTS, ElevenLabs, Kokoro-82M, Coqui and the operating-system voice. Falls back to the free voice if a paid engine fails. Footage & backgrounds - A separate stock-footage search for every scene (Pexels, Pixabay). Each candidate is scored by how well its own description matches the scene, the search engine's ranking, shape and length; portrait clips preferred, never reused across videos. - Gameplay and background videos (BACKGROUNDVIDEO): one continuous stretch of your Minecraft parkour, Subway Surfers or "satisfying" clip plays under the whole story, either full screen or split screen with the scene footage on top. - Fast pacing: scenes longer than 4.5 s are cut into several shots with different footage, each cut placed on a natural pause between words. - AI images per scene from OpenAI (gpt-image-1 / DALL·E 3) or Pollinations, or your own media/ folder. Ken Burns motion on photos, colour grades, transitions. Captions, sound & editing - Captions appear exactly when each word is spoken, with the current word highlighted. Key words and numbers get their own colour, and an emoji per scene pops up above them. 6 styles; Latin, Indic, Arabic, Thai and CJK scripts. - Sound effects made in code (nothing to license): a whoosh on each scene change, a pop as each text message lands, a low hit under the hook. They are mixed 11 dB under the measured voice. - Dialogues get speaker name tags and a colour per speaker; chat stories get an animated phone screen with typing indicators; Reddit-style stories open on a post card (community, poster, title, votes). - 9:16, 16:9, 1:1 or 4:5 output (--aspect), with captions and overlays sized for each shape. - Hook title, watermark, progress bar, end call-to-action, background music that ducks under the voice. - Broadcast-grade audio: gentle voice clean-up (rumble cut, de-esser, compression), then two-pass loudness normalisation that measures the mix and applies one steady gain, landing on −14 LUFS without pumping. - Voices without word timestamps get their phrase ends pinned to the real pauses in the audio, so captions stay in sync even without an aligner. - The cover image is the sharpest, best-exposed frame of the opening seconds, never a frame mid-transition. - Plain ffmpeg: each shot is prepared as a short segment, the soundtrack is mixed and normalised in its own pass, then one final encode joins them and adds everything above. No MoviePy, no ImageMagick, no GPU needed. Clipping (a free Opus Clip alternative) - Transcribes podcasts, interviews and streams locally with Whisper. The AI picks self-contained moments with a hook and a payoff, or only the ones that fit your brief (--prompt "every tip about sleep"). - Each clip has a virality score with the reason. It is edited with jump cuts (long pauses shortened, "um" and "uh" removed, lips kept in sync) and punch-in zoom between sentences. - Framing: face tracking (--crop face), the centre, or the whole picture over a blurred copy. Word-by-word captions are added too. Publishing & SEO - Uploads to YouTube, or schedules each video into your next free time slot. - TikTok, Instagram Reels and more (PUBLISHTO=youtube,tiktok,instagram): the same video goes out with a caption written for each network, at the same publish slot, through Upload-Post or Instagram's own API. Each network's result is saved, and a retry only re-sends what failed. - Localised titles and descriptions (LOCALIZEMETADATA=es,pt,hi), so viewers see the video under a title in their own language, and optional caption-track upload (UPLOADCAPTIONS) so YouTube can index every word. - Quota-aware queue, AI-content disclosure, playlists, privacy, made-for-kids flag. - Every video also gets a cover image, SRT subtitles and a metadata file for cross-posting. Workflow - Autopilot loop, one-off videos, bulk batches with parallel workers, several channels from separate settings files. - Studio web app: create, draft and edit, and watch every stage live (pushed instantly, with a percentage and a time-left estimate learned from your machine). Cancel a running job, browse and play the library, plan ideas, clip videos and read channel stats. STUDIOPASSWORD protects it when it runs on a server. - REST API for n8n, Zapier, cron or your own scripts (docs/api.md), a Google Colab notebook, and docker compose for servers. - A live progress line in the terminal, and a voice cache so re-rendering an edited script only voices the lines that changed. - MCP server: ask Claude Desktop, Claude Code or Cursor to make, clip or upload videos. - Learns from your channel (opt-in): view counts of your uploads show the AI what works for your audience, and the format of each new video is chosen by Thompson sampling over your own results. stats tells you whether the retention score actually predicts your views (Spearman correlation) and which publish hours did best. - Sound effects, key-word captions and the post card work as usual. Use only gameplay you recorded yourself or have the rights to reuse. --- ✂️ Clip podcasts into Shorts (free Opus Clip alternative) bash pip install faster-whisper # free, local transcription (or set OPENAIAPIKEY) purffle-shorts clip podcast.mp4 --count 3 # fill the frame purffle-shorts clip interview.mp4 --crop face # follow the speaker (pip install opencv-python-headless) purffle-shorts clip talk.mp4 --count 5 --crop blur # whole picture over a blurred copy purffle-shorts clip episode.mp4 --prompt "the funniest moments" # only the moments that fit a brief purffle-shorts clip " --count 3 # URLs need: pip install yt-dlp It works like Opus Clip, Klap or Vidyo.ai, but locally, with no per-minute fees and no watermark beyond your channel name. The video is transcribed with word timings. The LLM reads the timestamped transcript and picks moments of 20–58 s (--min-seconds, --max-seconds) that open with a hook and end on a complete thought, or only those matching your --prompt. Each moment gets a title, hashtags and a virality score with the reason. Each clip is cut on sentence boundaries, cropped to 9:16, captioned word by word with a hook title, and loudness-normalised. Edited like a pro editor would: jump cuts shorten pauses longer than CLIPMAXPAUSE (0.6 s) and remove "um" and "uh". Cuts land on frame boundaries and the sound is cut at exactly the same instants, so lips stay in sync however many cuts there are. Punch-in zoom changes the framing between sentences, at most every 2 seconds. Turn them off with --no-jump-cuts and --no-zoom (or CLIPJUMPCUTS=false, CLIPZOOM=false). Without an LLM it still works, with moments spread evenly over the video instead. Transcription uses WHISPERMODEL (auto picks large-v3-turbo on an NVIDIA GPU and small on a CPU) with voice-activity detection, so music and silence don't turn into invented words. --crop face finds the speaker's face twice a second (OpenCV's YuNet detector, a 230 KB model downloaded once) and keeps it in frame, switching framing only when the camera cuts. Clips upload like any other video when UPLOAD=true; add --no-upload to only cut them. Only clip videos you own or have permission to reuse. --- 🗓️ Ideas, sources and languages - What people search for: TOPICSOURCES=niche:2,search:2 mixes in questions people type into YouTube's search box about your niches ("why do octopuses have three hearts", "what happens when two oceans meet"); the AI answers the one that fits best. - Plan ahead: purffle-shorts plan --count 14 --niche "space" asks the AI for specific, true, non-repeating ideas with a format and an angle each, guided by real YouTube searches. ideas lists the queue (--add, --remove, --clear). Queued ideas are always made first; if a video fails, its idea goes back in the queue. - From a web page, a Reddit post or a document: make --url or make --from-file notes.md uses the text as the script's source material. A Reddit post link picks the Reddit story format automatically. - RSS: RSSFEEDS= and TOPICSOURCES=niche:3,rss:1. - Many languages: ALSOLANGUAGES=es,hi (or --also-lang) makes a translated copy of every video with a native voice, reusing the original's footage. Each copy is its own upload, linked to the original in the library. --- 🔍 SEO built in: real YouTube searches, localised titles, captions A Short that nobody searches for only lives as long as the Shorts feed shows it. PurffleShorts writes with search in mind: - Real search phrases (SEOKEYWORDS=true, the default): before writing, it asks YouTube's own search box what people type about the topic ("why do octopuses have three hearts", "octopus blue blood"). It hands those phrases to the script writer, which uses the matching ones word for word in the title, the first line of the description and the tags. Off-topic suggestions (documentaries, games, "in hindi" and so on), sensitive and adult ones are filtered out. They are saved in metadata.json as searchkeywords. - Topics people are looking for (TOPICSOURCES=search) and a planner that prefers ideas answering real searches. - Localised titles and descriptions (LOCALIZEMETADATA=es,pt,hi,fr): one extra LLM call translates the title and description, and the upload carries them as YouTube localizations. Viewers whose YouTube is in Spanish see the Spanish title, and so on, while the video stays one upload. - Caption tracks (UPLOADCAPTIONS=true): the exact subtitles are uploaded with the video, so YouTube has every spoken word to index (400 API units per video; run auth once more after turning it on). - Titles under 100 characters with #shorts, descriptions with a question that invites comments, 3–5 hashtags, tags kept under YouTube's 500-character limit, the right category, language and audio language, and the synthetic-media disclosure. --- 📊 Learn from your channel bash LEARNFROMSTATS=true YOUTUBEAPIKEY=... # optional: reads public stats without asking for more OAuth access purffle-shorts stats (and the Studio's Channel page) reads view, like and comment counts of the videos PurffleShorts uploaded: one API unit per 50 videos. With LEARNFROMSTATS=true the autopilot refreshes them twice a day and shows the LLM your best and worst performers (public for 48 hours or more) when it writes and plans. Without YOUTUBEAPIKEY, run auth once more to grant read access. Once 8 or more videos have stats, SCRIPTSTYLE=auto stops picking formats at random: each format's typical view count gets a statistical estimate that tightens as its videos come in, and the next format is drawn by Thompson sampling. Formats that work for your audience are chosen more often, and untried ones still get a fair chance. stats also checks the predictions against reality: the Spearman correlation between the Script Doctor's retention score and real views, median views per format, and the publish hours that did best. --- 🧠 AI models Set LLMPROVIDER and LLMMODEL in .env, or pass --provider / --model. Instagram's API can't schedule, so it posts right away. Without these keys, Instagram goes through Upload-Post | INSTAGRAMUSERID and INSTAGRAMACCESSTOKEN from a Meta app with Facebook Login for Business (permission instagramcontentpublish, a professional account) | | Facebook, Threads, X, LinkedIn, Bluesky, Pinterest | Upload-Post | Connect them to the same Upload-Post profile | Captions are written for each network: the title, the description and its hashtags, without #shorts, cut to each network's length. The cover frame is passed to Instagram. A network that fails never stops the others or the video. Its result is saved in metadata.json and shown in the Studio, and upload --id N (or Publish the rest in the Studio) re-sends only what didn't go out. > These integrations follow each service's published API and are covered by tests against recorded responses, but they have not yet been run against live TikTok and Instagram accounts. Please open an issue if a post doesn't go out as expected. - YTPRIVACY=public|unlisted|private. - PUBLISHTIMES=09:00,14:00,19:00 with TIMEZONE=Asia/Kolkata uploads each video as private and schedules it into the next free slot. Render in bulk, release on schedule. - Paced and quota-aware. YTDAILYLIMIT=6 uploads a day by default. That is a pace you choose, not the API's ceiling: uploads now have their own API bucket of 100 a day at 1 unit each (Google's quota table, updated 15 September 2026). Extra videos are queued, and so are videos YouTube refuses because the project or the channel hit a limit (quotaExceeded, uploadLimitExceeded); after a refusal nothing else is tried that day. On autopilot the queue is uploaded first after the reset at midnight Pacific time, and production waits instead of piling up. Without autopilot, run upload --pending after the reset. - SYNTHETICMEDIA=true sets YouTube's altered or synthetic content disclosure. MADEFORKIDS, PLAYLISTID and category (chosen by the AI) are set too. - Each video's folder holds short.mp4 (video.mp4 for 16:9), cover.jpg, captions.srt, script.json and metadata.json (including the retention score and where it was posted). KEEPVIDEOS=false deletes the MP4 once every destination has it. - Notifications: NOTIFYWEBHOOK= (or a Slack incoming webhook, or any URL for JSON) posts a message when a video is rendered, uploaded, scheduled, queued or fails. --- 💻 Command line bash python -m purffleshorts [options] # or purffle-shorts after pip install | Command | What it does | |---|---| | run | Autopilot loop. --count N, --once, --batch, --workers, --delay | | make | Make one video now. --topic "…", --url (web page or Reddit post), --from-file notes.md, --count N, --script file.json (your own script, no LLM) | | demo | Render a sample with no API keys (--style chat, dialogue or reddit for the story formats) | | clip | Cut a long video into Shorts: clip talk.mp4 --count 3 --crop center|face|blur --prompt "…" --no-jump-cuts --no-zoom | | plan / ideas | Let the AI plan ideas into the queue / list, add or remove queued ideas | | stats | Refresh and show view counts of your uploads | | mcp | Run as an MCP server for Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor… | | upload | --pending publishes rendered and queued videos, up to today's YTDAILYLIMIT; --id N publishes one, or re-sends only the networks that failed | | auth | Connect your YouTube channel | | doctor | Check ffmpeg and libass, LLM (including whether the Ollama model is pulled), voices, keys, footage sources, YouTube setup | | providers / voices | List LLM providers / free voices | | history | Everything made so far, with links | | studio | Local web app | Common options: --source queue|search|trending|wikipedia|reddit|rss|file|niche, --niche "space", --style facts|story|listicle|myth|quiz|explainer|motivational|news|dialogue|chat|reddit, --lang, --duration 45, --aspect 9:16|16:9|1:1|4:5, --also-lang es,hi, --provider, --model, --no-review, --tts, --voice, --voice-b, --visuals, --caption-style, --grade, --transition, --resolution, --background video.mp4, --layout full|split, --no-music, --no-sfx, --no-emoji, --no-upload, --privacy, --publish-times, --publish-to youtube,tiktok,instagram, --env-file. Your own script: every video folder has a script.json. Edit the narration, title or image prompts and render it again with make --script path/to/script.json. The files in examples/ show the format. Several channels: keep one settings file per channel (niche, voice, YTTOKENFILE, DATADIR) and run python -m purffleshorts run --env-file .env.channel2. Upgrading from 1.x: python YT.py, --once, --no-upload, --count N and the old SHORTS variables still work, and token.pickle is migrated to token.json automatically. Install the new requirements first. --- 🖥️ Studio (web app) bash python -m purffleshorts studio # opens - Create: topic, web page, idea queue or "surprise me"; eleven formats; language, length, aspect, voices, caption style (with a preview), grade, transitions, footage sources, a background video (full or split screen), sound effects, key-word colours, emoji, model, Script Doctor mode, extra languages, and publishing to YouTube, TikTok and Instagram. - Draft, then edit: the AI writes and reviews the script, you see the retention score and the problems it found, change any line, reorder or add scenes, switch speakers, then render exactly that script. - Live progress through topic, script, review, voice, footage, captions, render and upload, with the log. - Library: thumbnails with status, format, language and score; open one to play it, download the MP4 or captions, upload it, edit and re-render it, or delete it. - Ideas, Clip, Channel and System pages: plan and queue ideas, clip long videos (with a brief, jump cuts, zoom and face tracking; each clip shows its virality score), see views per video and per format, run the setup checks and copy the MCP config. The design is its own: warm paper and ink with one signal colour (a camera's red tally light), Schibsted Grotesk and JetBrains Mono bundled with the app, a light and a dark theme (or the system's), and layouts that work on a phone. The page needs no build step and loads nothing from a CDN. The Studio listens on localhost only, refuses requests for any other host name, sends a strict Content-Security-Policy, and every action needs a token (new each session, or fixed with STUDIOTOKEN). On a server, STUDIOPASSWORD puts a password on every page and API call. --- 🔗 REST API and automation (n8n, Zapier, cron) Everything the Studio does is a small JSON API, so n8n, Make, Zapier (through a webhook), a cron job or your own script can make, clip, plan and upload videos: bash STUDIOTOKEN=change-me purffle-shorts studio --no-browser curl -X POST localhost:8765/api/make -H "X-Studio-Token: change-me" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"topic": "why octopuses have three hearts", "style": "facts", "duration": 35}' # → {"job": 1} curl localhost:8765/api/jobs/1 # status, stage, percentage, time left, then the result with the video id curl -o short.mp4 localhost:8765/files/12/short.mp4 Jobs run one at a time in order. Follow them by polling GET /api/jobs/ , or listen to the Server-Sent Events stream at /api/events. docs/api.md lists every endpoint and field, with Python and curl examples and an n8n recipe that turns every new RSS item into a Short. --- 🤖 Use it from Claude and other AI apps (MCP) PurffleShorts is an MCP server too. Add it to Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor or any MCP client: json { "mcpServers": { "purffle-shorts": { "command": "purffle-shorts", "args": ["mcp"], "env": { "PURFFLEHOME": "/path/to/your/purffle/folder" } } } } Without installing anything, uv can run it straight from GitHub: use "command": "uvx" with "args": ["--from", "git+ "purffle-shorts", "mcp"]. PURFFLEHOME is the folder with your .env. Then ask things like "make a 30-second text story about a haunted smart speaker, in Spanish", "draft a dialogue about black holes and show me the script first", "clip my interview.mp4 into three Shorts" or "plan ten ideas about ancient Rome". Tools: makeshort (with a background video, layout, sound effects and emoji switches), draftscript, clipvideo (with a brief, jump cuts and zoom), planideas, listvideos, uploadvideo. Nothing is uploaded unless the request says so (upload: true); demo: true works without any keys. --- 🐳 Docker Each release is published as ghcr.io/chamanrajragu/purffle-shorts. With docker-compose.yml, a server, NAS or VPS runs the Studio, plus the autopilot if you want it: bash cp .env.example .env # add your keys and a STUDIOPASSWORD docker compose up -d # Studio on docker compose --profile autopilot up -d # also make and upload on schedule Or with plain Docker: bash docker run --rm -it --env-file .env -v "$PWD:/work" ghcr.io/chamanrajragu/purffle-shorts run docker build -t purffle-shorts . # build your own from this checkout Run auth once on your own computer so token.json exists in the mounted folder. For the Studio in Docker, publish the port on localhost only: docker run --rm -it --env-file .env -v "$PWD:/work" -p 127.0.0.1:8765:8765 purffle-shorts studio --host 0.0.0.0 --no-browser. Keep comments in .env on their own lines: --env-file reads a comment after a value as part of the value. --- ❓ FAQ Is PurffleShorts free? Yes. It is MIT-licensed and runs on your own computer. The default voices, Ollama models, faster-whisper and the Pexels and Pixabay APIs cost nothing. You only pay for paid APIs you choose to use, such as OpenAI, Claude or ElevenLabs. The Script Doctor adds two LLM calls per video (SCRIPTREVIEW=off to skip it). Can it make text-message stories, Reddit story videos or two-person conversations? Yes: --style chat renders an animated phone screen with messages popping in as each side's voice reads them, --style reddit opens on a Reddit-style post card and then tells the story with captions, and --style dialogue voices two people with name tags on the captions. Is there a free, open-source alternative to Opus Clip? purffle-shorts clip does the same job on your own computer. It transcribes a podcast, interview or stream, lets an LLM (a local Ollama model works) pick self-contained moments with a virality score, and cuts captioned 9:16 clips. The clips get jump cuts (pauses and ums removed, lips in sync), punch-in zoom and, with --crop face, face tracking. --prompt "…" tells it what to look for. There are no per-minute credits, and the only watermark is your channel name from CHANNELNAME (it reads PurffleStudios until you set it; WATERMARK=none removes it). How do I make Reddit story videos with Minecraft parkour or Subway Surfers gameplay? Put a gameplay video you may reuse in media/backgrounds/ and run purffle-shorts make --style reddit --background media/backgrounds/ (add --layout split for footage on top and gameplay below). A random, continuous stretch plays under the whole story, with the post card, narration, captions and sound effects on top. More. Can it remove silences and filler words from my podcast clips? Yes, by default: pauses longer than 0.6 s are shortened and "um" and "uh" are cut. Picture and sound are cut on the same frame boundaries, so lips stay in sync. CLIPMAXPAUSE sets the threshold, and --no-jump-cuts keeps everything. Does it add sound effects, emoji and highlighted key words like Submagic? Yes. Each video gets a whoosh on scene changes, a pop per text message and a hit under the hook, mixed 11 dB under the voice. The AI marks the key words of each scene, and those words and every number are drawn in colour. An emoji per scene pops up above the captions. Turn any of them off with SOUNDEFFECTS, CAPTIONEMPHASIS or CAPTIONEMOJI. Can I run it in Google Colab, on a server or from n8n? Yes. There is a Colab notebook, a docker-compose.yml for servers, and a REST API with an n8n recipe. Does it help my Shorts get found in YouTube search? It writes titles, descriptions and tags with the phrases YouTube's own search box suggests for the topic, can pick topics from what people search for, can translate titles and descriptions into other languages for viewers there (LOCALIZEMETADATA), and can upload the exact captions (UPLOADCAPTIONS). Details. No tool can promise views; a good hook and a satisfying payoff still matter most, and the Script Doctor grades both. How is it different from MoneyPrinterTurbo or ShortGPT? All three turn a topic into a Short. PurffleShorts adds a script review pass, text-message, dialogue and Reddit-style formats, long-video clipping, scheduled uploads through the official YouTube API, and an MCP server. See the comparison table for the details and where the others are ahead. Can Claude or another AI assistant make YouTube Shorts with this? Yes, through MCP: add PurffleShorts to an MCP client that runs local servers, such as Claude Desktop, Claude Code or Cursor (setup). Ask for a video in plain words and it writes, renders and, only if you ask, uploads it. Can it turn my podcast or stream into Shorts? Yes: purffle-shorts clip episode.mp4 --count 5 --no-upload (leave out --no-upload to upload the clips too). It needs faster-whisper (free, local) or an OpenAI key for the transcript. Can I try it without an API key? Yes. python -m purffleshorts demo renders a sample Short with no keys, and so does the Colab notebook. With Ollama installed, make writes scripts with a local model, also without a key. Does it work with ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek or Llama? Yes: OpenAI GPT models (including GPT-5 and the o-series), Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, DeepSeek, Mistral, xAI Grok, Llama through Groq, Together AI, Ollama or LM Studio, hundreds more through OpenRouter, and any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Can it post to TikTok or Instagram Reels? Yes: PUBLISHTO=youtube,tiktok,instagram. TikTok goes through Upload-Post, because TikTok's own API only lets audited apps publish public videos. Instagram can use its free official API or Upload-Post. Each network gets its own caption and the same publish slot (details). Every video is also a standard MP4 with a cover image and subtitles, if you would rather post it yourself. How many Shorts can it upload per day? Six by default (YTDAILYLIMIT). You can raise it: the YouTube API now gives uploads their own bucket of 100 a day. Posting many videos at once rarely helps a channel, so the default stays modest. Anything over the limit waits in a queue and uploads after the daily reset. Can I write or fix the script myself? Yes. Edit any video's script.json (or write one like examples/flamingos.json) and run make --script file.json. Which languages are supported? Set LANGUAGE (for example es, hi, ta, ar, ja) and the script, voice and caption font follow. The free voices cover 75 languages. ALSOLANGUAGES=es,hi publishes every video in those languages too. Do I need a GPU? No. Rendering uses ffmpeg on the CPU. A GPU only speeds up optional local models (Ollama, Kokoro, faster-whisper). Is automated uploading allowed? It uses the official YouTube Data API with your own Google sign-in, and sets YouTube's synthetic-content disclosure for you. You are responsible for what you publish: review the videos and follow YouTube's policies, including its monetisation rules on mass-produced, repetitive content. --- 🏗️ Tech stack | Component | Technology | |---|---| | Script | Any LLM: OpenAI-compatible HTTP (strict JSON schema where supported), plus the Anthropic SDK with structured outputs; a rubric-graded review pass and translation on the same providers | | Voice | edge-tts, OpenAI, ElevenLabs, Kokoro, Coqui, OS voices; multi-speaker joining; faster-whisper alignment or pause-anchored timing; a line cache | | Video | ffmpeg (xfade, vstack, zoompan, select/aselect jump cuts, sidechaincompress, two-pass loudnorm, silencedetect, libass, -progress), Pillow caption, emoji, chat and post-card renderers drawn on several threads; optional OpenCV face framing for clips | | Sound | Sound effects synthesised in Python (filtered noise and swept sines, no sample files), placed relative to the measured voice loudness | | Media | Pexels, Pixabay, local files and background videos, OpenAI Images, Pollinations, Twemoji; yt-dlp for clipping from URLs | | SEO | YouTube search suggestions (no key), YouTube localizations and caption tracks | | Upload | YouTube Data API v3, OAuth 2.0, resumable uploads, view statistics | | Studio | Python standard-library HTTP server with Server-Sent Events and a documented JSON API, vanilla JS/CSS, no build step | | Agents | MCP over stdio (standard library, no SDK) | | State | SQLite history in WAL mode (videos, topics, clips, uploads, schedule, idea queue, stats, stage timings), migrated automatically | --- 📁 Project structure purffle-shorts/ ├── YT.py # 1.x-compatible entry point (python YT.py) ├── purffleshorts/ │ ├── cli.py # commands: run, make, demo, clip, plan, ideas, stats, upload, auth, doctor, studio, mcp │ ├── pipeline.py # topic → script → review → voice → footage → render → upload → translations │ ├── llm.py # 12 LLM providers + fallback chain │ ├── script.py # prompt, JSON schema, Script Doctor, translation, clean-up, offline writer │ ├── planner.py # AI content planner → idea queue │ ├── clipper.py # long video → transcript → best moments → jump cuts, zoom, face framing → clips │ ├── tts.py # voice engines, two-speaker joining, word alignment │ ├── sfx.py # sound effects made in code (whoosh, pop, hit) │ ├── seo.py # YouTube search suggestions → topics and keywords │ ├── timing.py # word timing, scene timeline, caption chunks, SRT │ ├── media.py # Pexels / Pixabay / local / AI images, de-duplication │ ├── overlays.py # captions (Pillow + libass), key words, emoji, chat screen, post card, hook, CTA, fonts │ ├── render.py # ffmpeg segments, transitions, split screen, grading, audio mix │ ├── youtube.py # OAuth, upload, scheduling, quota │ ├── analytics.py # view counts → what the LLM learns from │ ├── notify.py # Discord / Slack / webhook messages │ ├── topics.py # idea queue, niches, YouTube searches, Trends, Wikipedia, Reddit, RSS, web pages, documents │ ├── history.py # SQLite history + migrations │ ├── doctor.py # setup checks (CLI and Studio) │ ├── mcpserver.py # MCP server over stdio │ ├── studio.py # local web app server + JSON API │ └── web/ # the Studio's HTML, CSS and JS ├── examples/ # ready-to-render scripts (make --script examples/flamingos.json) ├── notebooks/ # Google Colab notebook ├── tests/ # unit + offline end-to-end render tests (200+) ├── docs/ # REST API reference (api.md), screenshots, improvement notes ├── .env.example # the main settings, documented ├── Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml └── outputvideos/ # renders (gitignored) --- 🛠️ Troubleshooting | Problem | Fix | |---|---| | No LLM is configured | Add one key to .env (or start Ollama), then run doctor | | ollama model '…' is not pulled | ollama pull , or leave LLMMODEL empty to use a model you already have | | Every scene is a gradient | Add PEXELSAPIKEY / PIXABAYAPIKEY (both free) or put clips in media/ | | Pollinations returns HTTP 402 | Keyless use is now limited to about one image every few minutes. PurffleShorts skips it for the rest of that video; set POLLINATIONSAPIKEY or use Pexels/Pixabay | | clip says it needs a transcript | pip install faster-whisper (or set OPENAIAPIKEY); URLs also need pip install yt-dlp | | Setting problem: X='…' | A number setting in .env has a typo; the message names it and its default | | YouTube is not authorized | Run python -m purffleshorts auth | | Videos stay queued | Your YTDAILYLIMIT or one of YouTube's limits was reached. Autopilot uploads them after midnight Pacific; otherwise run upload --pending after the reset (or raise YTDAILYLIMIT) | | A video failed and the log is too short | Run with -v for full tracebacks (also written to data/logs/purffle.log) | | Wrong-looking non-Latin captions | Install an ffmpeg with libass (Homebrew and apt builds include it); doctor shows whether yours has it | | Too many cuts, or too few | MAXSHOTSECONDS sets the longest a single shot may last (default 4.5; 0 = one shot per scene) | | A job is taking too long in the Studio | Press Cancel on its card: ffmpeg stops at once, the rest at the next stage, and nothing half-made is kept | | The voice sounds too processed | VOICEENHANCE=false turns off the clean-up (rumble cut, de-esser, compression) | | Sound effects too loud or too quiet | SFXVOLUME=0.5 (quieter) or 2.0 (louder); SOUNDEFFECTS=false or --no-sfx turns them off | | No emoji in the video | They are downloaded once from the Twemoji CDN; without internet the video is made without them. CAPTIONEMOJI=false turns them off | | Clips feel cut too tightly | Raise CLIPMAXPAUSE (for example 1.0), or use --no-jump-cuts | | Upload-Post HTTP 403 for TikTok | TikTok isn't in Upload-Post's free plan. Upgrade, or remove tiktok from PUBLISHTO | | TikTok says draft | The video went to your TikTok inbox instead of going live (for example, the account needs to confirm it); open TikTok to publish it | | Instagram couldn't … check INSTAGRAMACCESSTOKEN | Instagram tokens expire: create a long-lived token again, or leave Instagram to Upload-Post | | A network failed but YouTube worked | purffle-shorts upload --id N re-sends only the networks that failed; the MP4 is kept until every destination has it | | BACKGROUNDVIDEO=… has no video files | Point it at a video file or a folder that contains .mp4, .mov, .mkv, .webm or .m4v files | | Transcription fails with metadataerrors | Fixed: audio is now decoded by ffmpeg before Whisper, so any PyAV version works. Update PurffleShorts | --- 🤝 Contributing Bug reports, ideas and pull requests are welcome. See CONTRIBUTING.md for the dev setup (tests run offline and render a real video), and CHANGELOG.md for what changed. Questions and ideas are welcome in Discussions once they are enabled, or as an issue. --- ⚠️ Disclaimer > This is an open-source automation tool for educational purposes. It needs your own API keys. Review AI-generated content before publishing, keep the synthetic-media disclosure on, and follow YouTube's Terms of Service and Community Guidelines. Not affiliated with YouTube, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Microsoft, Pexels, Pixabay, Pollinations or Reddit. --- Built by Chaman Raj Part of the Purffle ecosystem — PurffleTools · PurffleAI · Purffle.com --- 🧩 The Purffle toolset PurffleShorts is part of Purffle — a growing set of free, open-source tools built in the open. If this saved you time, please drop a ⭐ — it genuinely helps the project reach more people! | Tool | What it does | |------|--------------| | 🔄 Claude Multi | Run Claude Code with multiple accounts — auto-switch on the 5-hour limit · paid app, from $5/month | | 📐 Purffle Chartwright | Desktop chart analysis where the AI cannot invent a price | | 🎵 PurffleGrab | Free Spotify & YouTube downloader — MP3, MP4, 4K | | 🎥 PurffleVision | AI video creation — any topic to a finished video | | ⚡ PurffleShorts 👈 | Autonomous YouTube Shorts generator | | 📈 PurffleTrader | Crypto paper-trading bot — Binance, EMA + RSI | | 🤖 PurffleCopyBot | Copy-trading bot — mirror top Hyperliquid traders | 🌐 purffle.com · 💼 by Chaman Raj · ⭐ Star to support open-source --- Need Something Like This Built for You? I wrote this. I also write Python for other people — fixed price, agreed before I start. - Python automation — batch file processing, Excel/CSV cleaning, API pulls, scheduled reports, packaged as a .exe if you do not use Python · 1–5 days - Web scraping — clean data as Excel, CSV, JSON or Sheets, plus the reusable scraper · 1–4 days - Custom AI chatbots — trained on your own docs, full source code, no monthly fee · 2–7 days - Excel and Google Sheets — formulas, dashboards, macros, Apps Script · 1–4 days I only take work I can verify myself before delivering it — I run it on your real data first.
