Repository: bodrumundenizi-beep/free-ai-video-generator
    Description: Free Windows app that turns a script into a YouTube Short: stock footage, AI voice, auto-captions. No watermark.
    Language: Python
    Topics: ai-video, ai-video-generator, auto-captions, automation, faceless-youtube, llama-cpp, local-llm, open-source, python, qwen, short-form-content, stock-footage, text-to-video, text-to-video-free, text-to-video-generation, tts, video-automation, video-generator, windows, youtube-shorts

    README:
    AI Video Studio 🌐 Website · ⬇ Download for Windows A professional-grade automated video generation tool that turns written scripts into fully edited, high-quality videos. Pick the visuals in words, write the narration, and it fetches matching stock footage from Pexels, generates a neural voiceover, and renders a 1080p or 720p MP4 in portrait or landscape. Made from a six-scene script: footage, voice and captions are automatic. Features - Paste text, get a video: On Home, press Make new video, paste an article, a tip or your notes and press Make video. - Storyboard: See the video as a card per scene before it is made. Change a line, swap a clip, make another AI picture, reorder scenes, and hear any line read out. - Dashboard: How many videos you made and how long they run, a chart of the last 8 weeks, the voice and shape you use most, recent videos, storage, and what's set up. - My videos: Every video you make is kept on the My videos page. Open it again in the Storyboard, change it, make a copy in the other shape or voice, rename it, search. An unfinished Storyboard is kept as a draft. - Tell it what to change: Type "make it shorter" or "more exciting start" and the built-in AI rewrites the script; you see what changed before anything is rendered. - Paste any text, get a script: Paste plain text, say who the video is for and how long it should be, and a built-in open-source AI writes the script. It runs on your PC: no account, no key, nothing sent anywhere. - Automated Stock Footage: Automatically fetches relevant video clips from Pexels or Pixabay, and picks the one whose description fits the scene best. With the Smart writer, each clip is looked at before the video is made and swapped if it shows something else. - Drawn styles: Blackboard chalk or flat-colour drawing, each scene drawn on screen. Fast on any PC. - Facts from Wikipedia: Ask for "top 5..." and the Smart writer reads Wikipedia instead of guessing. - Templates and batches: Start from Tech tip, Story, Top 5 or Motivation, or make several videos in one go. - Moving AI pictures (beta): With a graphics card, an AI picture can become a short moving clip. - Music included: Eight public-domain tracks, picked by the video's mood. - Two versions in one go: Optionally render the same script twice with different clips, and keep the better one. - Pick a length: Fit the video to 15, 30 or 60 seconds, or make a long video of 3, 5 or 10 minutes in chapters, with a live estimate as you type. - Neural AI Voices, on your PC: 20 natural-sounding male and female voices from an open-source speech model that runs offline. No account, no key, no service that can be switched off. - AI pictures (optional): With a good graphics card, an open-source image model on your PC draws a picture for the scenes stock footage has nothing for. - Animated cards: Key combos like Win + V, big numbers and short lists are drawn over the footage, because no stock clip can show them. - Smart Script Parser: Automatically reads your script line-by-line using Visual: and Voice: tags. - Windows 11 Fluent interface: Settings-app style segmented controls, smooth page transitions, dark and light themes with Mica, and live render progress. - Auto-captions: The spoken words are burned into the video, a few at a time, with the word being said highlighted. An .srt subtitle file is saved too. - Watch it straight away: When a render finishes, the video plays inside the app, with sound. - Ready to post: Every video gets a thumbnail and a suggested title, description and tags, with Copy buttons. Nothing is posted for you. - Thumbnail editor: Change the thumbnail with text, arrows, circles, stickers and Pexels or Pixabay photos. - Your photos in the video: Add up to 10 photos to Make new video. The app sees what is in each one, writes the script around them and puts each photo in the scene about it. - Image editor: Paint a part of a photo and Change it with words ("make the car green"), Erase it, or Remove the background, all on your PC. - Other languages: Make the same video in Spanish, French, Italian, Portuguese or Hindi. - Sound effects: A soft pop when a card appears, made by the app itself. - Portrait or landscape: 9:16 for Shorts and TikTok, 16:9 for YouTube, at 1080p or 720p. - End-to-End Automation: Fetches, generates, matches duration, and stitches everything into a final .mp4. Download Get the latest release: | | | |---|---| | AIVideoStudio-x.y.z-setup.exe | Normal install. Adds a Start menu entry and an uninstaller. Installs for your user only, so it never asks for administrator rights. | | AIVideoStudio-x.y.z-portable.zip | No install. Unzip anywhere and run AIVideoStudio.exe. | No Python, no pip, no separate FFmpeg install — everything is in the download. Updating: the app tells you when a newer version is out. Press Update now: the app downloads the new version, checks it, puts it over the old one and reopens. This works for the installed version and, from 4.2.1, the portable one (unless its folder is somewhere Windows won't let it write, such as Program Files). Your settings, API keys, projects and the Smart writer are kept. (Running from source still needs all three; see below.) The AI models are a separate 2.9 GB download: the voice (0.4 GB) and the Smart writer (2.5 GB). The installer fetches both during setup; the portable version fetches the voice the first time you make a video and the Smart writer the first time you use New from text. They are downloaded once and kept when you update the app. See New from text below. System requirements | | Needs | |---|---| | Windows | 10 or 11, 64-bit | | Memory (RAM) | 16 GB. The Smart writer uses about 5 GB while it writes; if the PC is short of memory, the app uses Quick split. | | Disk | About 3.5 GB: the app (0.3 GB) and its AI models (2.9 GB). AI pictures add 4.2 GB. | | Graphics card | Not needed. It only speeds up the optional extras: AI pictures, Moving pictures and My voice. | Windows will warn you the first time These builds are not code-signed, because a signing certificate costs several hundred dollars a year. The project has applied to the SignPath Foundation for free open-source code signing and is waiting for a reply. Until then, SmartScreen will show "Windows protected your PC", where the only obvious button is Don't run. Click More info → Run anyway. You can confirm you have the real file by checking its hash against SHA256SUMS.txt on the release page: powershell Get-FileHash .\AIVideoStudio-5.2.0-setup.exe -Algorithm SHA256 The quick way 1. On Home, press Make new video, paste your text into the From text box and press Make video. 2. Check the three answers the app suggests (who it is for, how long, where it will be posted) and press Write script, then Use this script. 3. The Storyboard opens: one card per scene, with its picture and its line. Change what you don't like, then press Make video. Tick Make it straight away next to Make video to skip step 3. Templates: above the box, pick Tech tip, Story, Top 5 or Motivation and the questions in step 2 come already answered (who it is for, how long, captions, cards, the music's mood). Top 5 also writes the video as a countdown. Several at once (on the Make new video page): paste one text or topic per block, with an empty line between them, and press Start. Each becomes its own script and video, one after another, and its own card on the My videos page. Up to 20 at a time. Storyboard The Storyboard is the same video as the script, shown as cards. Everything you change there is written into the script, and the other way round. | On each card | What you can do | |---|---| | The picture | Another clip steps through up to six stock clips. Make picture / Make another draws the AI picture now, and the video then uses exactly that one. Use an AI picture and Use a stock clip switch the scene between the two. | | The line | Edit it in place. Hear it reads that one line in the chosen voice. | | The search words or picture description | Edit in place; the picture reloads. | | The card | Add, change or remove a Win + V style card. | | Up, Down, Add, Delete | Change the order, add a scene, remove one. | Undo and Redo (or Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y) step back and forward through up to 50 changes made in the Storyboard, including a "Change it" rewrite. Timeline: under the cards, one block per scene, as wide as the scene is long. Drag a block's right edge to set how long that scene lasts (half-second steps, 1 to 30 s; it turns yellow if the line no longer fits), double-click it to go back to automatic, click it to jump to its card. Tell it what to change At the bottom of the Storyboard, and in the window that opens when a video is finished, there is a box: Say what to change. Type it in your own words and press Change it: - "make it shorter", "make the start more exciting", "sound more serious", "write it for kids" - "remove the part about pinning", "put the last scene first" - "the third picture should be a cat on a laptop", "add a line telling people to subscribe" The Smart writer rewrites the script, the Storyboard marks the scenes that changed, and nothing is rendered until you press Make video. Scenes that did not change keep their clips and pictures. It changes the script only: not the voice, the captions or the music, which you set on the Storyboard. It needs the Smart writer download, and it is a small AI model: if it changes nothing, or the wrong thing, say it another way or edit the card yourself. Ctrl+Z on the Script editor brings the old lines back. My videos Every video you make is saved as a project: its script, its settings (shape, voice, captions, look, length, music) and its AI pictures. The My videos page shows them as cards, newest first, with a search box for titles and scripts. | On each card | What it does | |---|---| | Open | Puts the video back in the Storyboard with its settings and AI pictures, ready to change and make again. | | Change it | Opens it and takes you to the Say what to change box. | | Play, Show in folder | The video file. | | Make a copy | The same video in the other shape (9:16 or 16:9) or with another voice. Same shape: the AI pictures are reused. Another shape: new pictures are made. | | Rename | Type a new name and press Enter. | | Delete | Removes the project and its saved pictures. Your video file is kept. | A Storyboard you leave without making the video is kept too, as a Draft card. Videos made with versions before 4.2 are not listed: their scripts were not saved. First run The very first time, a short four-screen tour shows how the app is used. It is not shown again after an update; Settings → Help & about → Show the tour brings it back. The app needs one free stock footage key, from either Pixabay or Pexels. Neither is required: one of the two is enough. The first time you open the app, a Welcome window walks you through it: choose Pixabay or Pexels, open its page, copy your key, paste it in, and press Test key to check it works. You can reopen the window later from Settings → Help & about → Setup guide, or paste a key into Settings. With both keys set, the app searches Pexels and Pixabay together and gives each scene the clip that fits it best, from either site (Settings → Footage keys → With both keys can ask one site first instead). Scripts that only use your own files (see local: below) need no key at all. No key at all? If you have downloaded AI pictures (they need a good graphics card), the app draws a picture for every scene and never asks for a key. When the video is done it mentions once that a free key would add real video clips; tick Don't show again and it won't. Keys are stored in plain text in %APPDATA%\AIVideoStudio\settings.json. New from text You don't have to write the script format by hand. Paste your text in Make new video, or press New from text on the Script editor (Settings → Advanced): An idea works too. Type a short request instead of a text, such as "write a scary story about being followed at night" or "make a video about black holes", and the Smart writer writes it from scratch: for a story, something happens in every scene (a start, rising tension, a turn, an ending). A pasted text is rewritten as before. 1. Paste your text and press Analyse. Any plain text works: notes, an article, a list. 2. Check the answers. The app reads the text and picks who the video is for (what it is about, the age group), how long it should be and its shape. You also choose where it will be posted. Change anything that isn't right. 3. Write script. Read the result, press Write again if you want a different version, then Use this script to put it in the editor. Your photos Press + Add photos under the text to add up to 10 photos (.png .jpg .jpeg .webp .bmp). When you press Analyse, the Smart writer looks at each one and writes a sentence about what is in it ("A red tractor is driving through a field of green wheat"). Fix the sentence if it's wrong, or type your own. - Use in the video (on by default): the photo is shown in the scene that talks about it, once. Switch it off and the photo only tells the writer what to write about. - Change it... opens the Image editor on that photo; the picture you keep is used instead. - Quick split puts each photo in the scene whose words match its sentence best, and spreads the rest evenly. - When the video is saved, the photos are copied into its project, so it still works if you move or delete the originals. Looking at photos is done on your PC by SmolVLM 500M (Apache 2.0 licence), part of the Smart writer's download (0.5 GB more). If you downloaded the Smart writer before 5.0, Settings → Smart writer offers just the photo part. It takes about a second a photo with a graphics card. There are two writers: | | Smart writer | Quick split | |---|---|---| | What it does | Rewrites and shortens your text to fit the length, opens with a hook, and picks search words for each scene | Keeps your words exactly as written, splits them into scenes, and guesses search words from each sentence | | Speed | About 10 to 60 seconds | Instant | | Needs | A one-time 3 GB download and 16 GB of RAM | Nothing | If a text is too long for the length you chose, the Smart writer shortens it. Quick split leaves out the least important sentences, lists them with a Put back button, and offers the shortest length that keeps everything. What the audience changes: the voice, the speaking pace and how short the scenes are. The Smart writer is also told who it is writing for, but expect the wording to change only a little between audiences. About the Smart writer The Smart writer is Qwen3 4B, an open-source language model (Apache 2.0 licence), run on your PC by llama.cpp (MIT licence). - Private: your text never leaves your computer. No account and no key. - One download: 3 GB (the writer, and SmolVLM 500M for photos), saved in %LOCALAPPDATA%\AIVideoStudio\models. A cancelled download carries on from where it stopped. Settings → Smart writer shows its state and can download or repair it. - Memory: it uses about 5 GB while it writes and gives it back straight after. If the PC is short of memory, too slow, or anything else goes wrong, the app uses Quick split and tells you why. - Graphics card: turn on Settings → Use the graphics card to run it on a dedicated NVIDIA, AMD or Intel card instead of the processor. On an RTX 4060 a script takes about 3 seconds instead of about 20. A new install turns it on when the PC has graphics it can use (Intel and AMD graphics built into the processor count); an update keeps your choice. It needs about 3 GB of video memory, and goes back to the processor by itself if the card can't be used. - It can be wrong. It is a small model. Read the script before you render: it sometimes changes a detail, such as "every workday" becoming "every day". Stock clips checked before the video With the Smart writer downloaded, Settings → Smart writer → Check stock clips looks at every stock clip a video will show, before anything is made: - The writer reads what Pexels or Pixabay says the clip shows; a clear "no" (roast pork for "roast thermometer") is skipped at once. - The photo model looks at the clip's preview picture, and the writer judges what it saw. A clip that shows something else is swapped for the next one, so you never see clips switching. - After 4 clips with no fit the scene becomes an AI picture (at most 1 scene in 10, if AI pictures are downloaded). Without AI pictures, one window before the video asks about those scenes: Use this or Try the next clip. - A long line that shows two clips gets both checked. Clips you picked in the Storyboard are left alone. It adds time before the video starts: on an RTX 4060 about 40 seconds for a 60 second video and about 3 minutes for a 3 minute one. On the processor it is about 4 times slower, so it is on by default only when the Smart writer uses the graphics card. The models are small and still miss some clips. Writing a script Every line starts with Visual: or Voice:, in pairs. Visual: is the Pexels search; Voice: is what gets spoken over it. One pair is one scene. Visual: frustrated person typing laptop Voice: Did you know you are copying and pasting completely wrong on Windows? Visual: hands on glowing keyboard Voice: Press the Windows key and the letter V to unlock your clipboard history. See examplescript.txt for a full worked example. Optional per-scene settings Any scene can add these lines after its Visual:, in any order. Scripts without them work exactly as before. Visual: hard drive Voice: Your PC is hoarding gigabytes of junk. Duration: auto Zoom: in Visual: local:C:/Users/me/recordings/taskmgr.mp4 Voice: Here is the fix. Open Task Manager. Duration: 4s | Line | Values | If left out | |---|---|---| | Duration: | auto, or seconds like 4.5s. A set duration is exact — a longer voice line is cut short, with a warning in the log. | auto: the scene lasts as long as its voice line, plus padding | | Padding: | seconds like 0.5s of pause after the voice line (ignored when Duration: is set) | the Scene padding setting | | Zoom: | in, out, or none — a slow 1.0× → 1.1× Ken Burns zoom | a subtle zoom, stronger on photos and still footage | | Card: | text drawn over the footage — see Cards below | no card | A scene with no Voice: line is a silent shot and needs a Duration:, e.g. a logo held for Duration: 2s. When a voice line runs longer than 6 seconds and has no set duration, the scene cuts between two different clips halfway through, to keep the pace up. Scenes join with a short 0.3 s crossfade. Cards Stock footage cannot show a keyboard shortcut or a figure, so a scene can put it on screen with a Card: line. What you write picks the look: | You write | You get | |---|---| | Card: Win + V (parts joined by +) | keycaps, one per part | | Card: $120,000 or Card: $120,000 | after 30 years | a big line, with a small one under it | | Card: Paste; Pick a length; Done (parts split by ;) | a list, the items appearing one by one | Anything else is shown as a big title. The card pops in as its scene starts and fades out as it ends, in the half of the frame the captions are not using, in your caption colour. New from text adds cards by itself when a line says to press keys ("Press the Windows key and V") or is about a dollar amount, a percentage or a large number. At most half the scenes get one. They arrive as Card: lines in the script, so you can edit or delete them; Settings → Add cards automatically turns this off. AI pictures (optional) Stock sites have no clip of a clipboard history window or a robot holding your product. The AI pictures tab in Settings can download an open-source image model (Z-Image Turbo) that draws those pictures on your own PC. Nothing is sent anywhere, and nothing is installed unless you press Download there. - What it runs on: | Your PC | What to expect | |---|---| | A graphics card with about 8 GB of video memory | Best. A picture takes around 20 seconds on an RTX 4060. | | No graphics card, or one that can't make the picture | The app makes a smaller picture on the processor, which can take several minutes, and remembers that for next time. | Integrated graphics (the graphics built into many laptop processors) haven't been tested yet. A picture needs about 5 GB of free memory at full size, and the app makes a smaller one with less. - No stock footage key needed. With AI pictures downloaded and no Pexels or Pixabay key, the app draws a picture for every scene. The welcome screen still offers to add a key; press Skip for now. - The download is about 4.2 GB, once. It also uses the Smart writer's file. - Ask for a picture in any script with ai: and a description: Visual: ai: a laptop screen showing a list of copied text, a hand on the keyboard Voice: Press the Windows key and V to open your clipboard history. The picture is made while the video is made and gets the same slow zoom as a photo. - New from text writes the descriptions for you. Under Use AI pictures for choose the scenes stock footage can't show (the default), every scene, or only your own ai: lines. Look sets one style for the whole video. - If a picture can't be made (not enough free memory, for example), that scene uses stock footage instead and the Log says why. Speed. The Speed row in the AI pictures tab chooses the picture size: Fast (384 x 672), Balanced (480 x 848) or Best (576 x 1024). Smaller pictures are made much faster and enlarged to the video's size once, carefully, before the slow zoom. On a PC without a graphics card the app starts on Fast, never goes above it on the processor, gives only the first two scenes an AI picture by default, and before a long render says how long it will take and offers to make two pictures and use them again. Test speed times a tiny picture a few ways on the processor and keeps the fastest; Copy results puts the numbers on the clipboard. Settings → AI picture threads sets the thread count by hand. Make pictures on chooses where pictures are made: Auto (the graphics card, and the processor if the card fails), Graphics card only (a scene whose picture fails uses a stock clip), or Processor only. You are responsible for what you ask it to draw and for how you use the pictures. Image editor: change, erase, remove the background The Image editor page has three tools, and one habit for all of them: paint first, then act. Open a photo, paint over a part of it with the brush (Paint, Rub out, Brush size, Clear), and pick a tool: - Change: type what the painted part should become and press Change it. Only that part changes; the rest of the photo stays exactly as it was. Name the thing: "make the car green" works, "make it green" may not. Select all paints the whole photo, to change all of it ("make it look old"). How much (Little, Some, A lot) sets how far it may go. - Erase: paint over something and its shadow, and press Erase. It's gone in a few seconds. With AI pictures downloaded, a second version follows about 20 seconds later, touched up to look like a real photo; both stay in the row, so you can pick. Very big things (a third of the photo or more) can leave a smudge. - Remove background: press Remove and the background goes. To fix it, brush on the result: Paint brings a part back, Rub out removes more. Save as picture keeps it see-through as a PNG; in a video or as a thumbnail layer it goes on white. Every try stays in the row underneath, and Try again makes another version. Save as picture saves it (Pictures folder by default), and Use in a new video opens Make new video with it added as a photo. The same editor opens from Change it... on a photo in Make new video, and from Change with words... on a thumbnail's background or picture (Undo puts the old one back). What it needs: Erase and Remove background work without a graphics card: about 3 and 7 seconds a photo on the processor. The first time you use each one, it asks to download its model once (106 MB for Erase, 91 MB for Remove background); after that it works offline, and an update keeps it. Change, and Erase's touched-up version, use the AI pictures model (see above): about 20 seconds with a graphics card, a few minutes without one. Erase uses LaMa and Remove background BiRefNet, both open source; see THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md. Drawn styles: Blackboard and Drawing Style (next to the templates in Make new video, and in the Storyboard's This video box): Blackboard turns every scene into white chalk lines on a dark board, like a teacher explaining; Drawing turns it into a simple drawing with flat colours and dark outlines. Each scene draws itself on screen in its first two seconds, then stays. The Explainer template uses Blackboard. It is made from the picture each scene already has (a stock clip's middle frame, an AI picture or your own image) with simple image maths, not AI, so it is quick on any PC: about 2 seconds a scene here, and the whole render is no slower than a normal one. Busy stock clips make busy drawings; simple pictures make the best ones. Facts from Wikipedia When you type an idea that asks for facts ("top 5...", "fastest...", "latest..."), the Smart writer first reads the best matching Wikipedia pages and is told to use only what they say; the window names the pages. Only the search words leave your PC. It is much better than the model's own guesses, but not perfect (rankings and "newest" models can still come out wrong), so read a fact video before posting it. Settings → Look facts up on Wikipedia turns it off. Moving pictures (beta, graphics card only) In the AI pictures tab in Settings, Make AI pictures move downloads Wan 2.2 TI2V 5B (8.5 GB, Apache 2.0), and Which pictures move turns an AI picture into a short moving clip instead of a still with a slow zoom: the first AI scene of each video, or every AI scene. The picture is the clip's first frame, so the scene still shows what you saw in the Storyboard; the clip plays forward and then backward, so it fills a longer scene without a jump. Measured on an RTX 4060 (8 GB): about 1.5 minutes per clip, 6.9 GB of graphics memory. It needs a graphics card: on the processor it stays off, and the scene keeps its still picture. If a clip can't be made, the still picture is used and the video is made anyway. My voice (beta, NVIDIA graphics card only) Settings → My voice → Make my voice: read six sentences out loud, and the app speaks your scripts in a voice like yours, made with KittenTTS 2 from about 27 seconds of your recording. The first time it installs the voice pack (about 7 GB, about 15 minutes here: PyTorch for your graphics card and the voice model), which can be stopped and carried on later, and removed again in the same window. Then it plays a test line, and My voice (beta) appears in the voice list. Measured on an RTX 4060 (8 GB): about 26 s to load once per video, then about as long as the speech itself (20.8 s of speech in 20.7 s), 4.9 GB of graphics memory. It needs an NVIDIA card with 6 GB or more: on the processor it is about 10 times slower than the video, so on other PCs the button explains why it isn't available. In a test it sounded "about 70 percent" like the person; a quiet room and your normal reading speed help most. Captions follow the words closely but not exactly, because the timings are estimated. If a line can't be made, that line uses the normal voice and the video is made anyway. Your recording stays on your PC. Show it on my PC (beta) A tip video recorded by the app itself: hook, Win + I, search, the page, then back. Make new video → Windows tip: type a Windows tip ("how to turn on night light") and press Record. The app finds the page itself while it records: Settings' search box (with a Win + I card), the taskbar's menu for Task Manager, or the Run box (Win + R) for Control Panel pages and tools. Don't touch the mouse while it does; if you do, it opens the page directly instead. A small box, left out of the recording, says what to click. When the tip is a simple on/off switch (night light, dark mode, Game Mode...), the app asks "OK to change this?" and only after Yes clicks the switch itself, then switches it back right after the recording and checks it. It writes the switch down before clicking, so if the app or the PC stops halfway, the next start puts it back. Switches that could cut you off or need a restart (screen, network, mouse, accessibility, updates, accounts...) are never clicked by the app: you click those, and the app walks you through switching them back. Your account name, email and picture are hidden in the video. Admin pages (firewall, registry...) aren't recorded. Your own footage and images Start a Visual: with local: to use a file instead of stock footage — a screen recording, your own b-roll, a screenshot or a photo: Visual: local:C:/Users/me/Videos/demo.mp4 Visual: local:screenshots/settings.png Videos: .mp4 .mov .mkv .webm .avi .m4v (their own sound is dropped). Images: .png .jpg .jpeg .webp .bmp. A relative path is looked up in the folder the video is being saved to. Every local: file is checked before anything is downloaded, so a typo fails straight away. Background music The app comes with eight public-domain tracks (CC0: free to use in any video, including monetised ones, no credit needed). With the track set to Auto (fits the video), the app picks one by what the video is about: calm for tech and money, upbeat for motivation and kids, dramatic for stories. Music is on by default for new installs. Turn on Settings → Background music and pick a track. It plays at about 25% volume in the pauses and dips to about 9% whenever the voice is speaking, easing down just before each line and back up after. Drop tracks into Documents\AI Video Studio\Music (Open folder), or Browse for any audio file. Thumbnail, title, description and tags After every render the app saves name.thumbnail.jpg beside the video: the sharpest frame from a pause between lines (so no caption is in the way) with the title across it, in the video's shape (720x1280 or 1280x720). The Render complete window has Open thumbnail, and the project card shows it. The Storyboard's Thumbnail tab (next to Setup and Log, or Edit thumbnail in the Thumbnail box) is the thumbnail editor, before or after the video is made. It starts from the automatic thumbnail and works in layers: - Background: any scene's picture, or a picture from your PC, with blur, darken, brightness and contrast so the words stand out. - Text: as many boxes as you like, with font, size, colour, outline, shadow, glow, a dark band behind, and tilt. - Draw: brush, arrow, circle and box, in YouTube red or any colour. - Stickers: 30 emoji and arrows, with an outline and a glow. - Photos: search Pexels and Pixabay photos with your footage keys, or add a picture from your PC. A stock photo's credit is added to the video's credits file. Drag a layer to move it (it snaps to the middle), drag its corners to resize it and the round handle to turn it. Arrow keys nudge it, Delete removes it, Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y undo and redo. Save keeps the thumbnail with the video's project: the Storyboard shows it and the video uses it (a copy in the other shape gets the automatic one). Reset to automatic goes back to the one the app makes. The Thumbnails page in the sidebar lists every video's thumbnail, marked Edited or Automatic. Edit opens the editor right there (Back returns to the list), with pictures taken from the made video; Start over begins from a plain background; Save as picture puts a copy wherever you want it. Saving an edit of a video that is already made also replaces its .thumbnail.jpg, so it is ready to upload without making the video again. + New 16:9 thumbnail and + New 9:16 thumbnail make free thumbnails that belong to no video, kept on the same page. The same window shows a title, a short description and tags for posting, written by the Smart writer from what the video says, each with a Copy button. They are also saved as name.upload.txt. Without the Smart writer the first line is the title and the search words are the tags. Nothing is uploaded or posted anywhere. Other languages Make it in another language (on a project card, and in the window that opens when a video is finished) makes a copy of the video in Spanish, French, Italian, Portuguese (Brazil) or Hindi. The Smart writer translates the lines; the pictures, clips and cards stay; the voice and the captions change to that language. The copy opens in the Storyboard first, because the Smart writer is a small AI: its translations are understandable but have mistakes, so read the lines (or have someone who speaks the language read them) before making the video. Each language has its own voices in the voice list (Spanish, Italian, Portuguese and Hindi a female and a male one, French a female one). Cuts on the beat and smart framing Settings → Cuts on the beat, smart framing (on by default). With music on, each change of scene moves to the nearest beat of the track (at most a quarter of a second, and never before the line has been said). And when a wide clip is cut down for a Short, or the slow zoom moves in, the frame heads toward the part of the picture with the most detail (a person, hands, a screen) instead of always the middle. Sound effects Settings → Sound effects (on by default): a short pop when a card appears, quiet under the voice. The app makes these sounds itself, so there is nothing to download and no licence to worry about. Start and end cards Settings → Start and end cards: a 2-second card with your channel name before every video, and one after it (default "Subscribe for more"). Both are off until you turn them on. They are added when the video is made, not written into your script. Both shapes at once Make both shapes on the Storyboard makes the video in its shape, then in the other one (9:16 and 16:9), saved side by side as name.mp4 and name (16x9).mp4 and kept in the same project. AI pictures are made again for the second shape. Voices Pick a voice on the Storyboard, set its Speed (Slower, Normal, Faster: Slower suits long videos), and press ▶ Preview Voice to hear it before rendering. All voices are free — no account or key needed. The voices are spoken on your PC by Kokoro, an open-source speech model (a one-time 0.4 GB download), so they work with no internet. Up to version 3.7 the app used Microsoft Edge's online voices; that service stopped answering in October 2026. The old voices are still there under Settings → Voice → Use Microsoft's online voices, in case it comes back. | Group | Voices | Delivery | |---|---|---| | Viral / Shorts | Max, Cole, Zoe, Mia (US) | fast and punchy, very short pauses | | Tech / Short-Form Hype | Guy, Jenny, Steffan (US) | a bit faster and brighter, short pauses | | Deep / Storyteller | Christopher, Eric, Roger (US) | a bit slower and lower, longer pauses | | Professional / Tutorial | Aria, Andrew, Ava (US) | clear, even pace | | Accents & Regional | Ryan, Sonia, William (UK) | natural pace | | Classic (low quality) | the four voices from earlier versions | read exactly as before, no studio processing | The first four groups get studio processing: natural breath pauses at commas and full stops, then broadcast mastering — low-end warmth, compression so every word is audible, and loudness set to −14 LUFS, the level YouTube Shorts, Reels and TikTok play at. Two versions Set Versions to 2 and the app renders the script twice: the same voice and captions, different clips in every stock scene. They are saved as name.mp4 and name (version 2).mp4, each with its own subtitles and credits file, and the Render complete window lets you play both. The voice is made once, so two versions take well under twice as long as one. Video length The Storyboard shows about how long your script will be next to Length, and updates as you change it. It is an estimate: the voice paces every line a little differently. Set Length to 15 s, 30 s, 60 s, 3 min, 5 min or 10 min to fit the video to that length. The app adjusts the pauses between scenes first. If that is not enough, it speeds the voice up or slows it down by at most 15%, keeping its pitch, and the captions follow. A script that is far too long or too short is rendered as close as it gets, and the Log tells you roughly how many words to cut or add. Scenes with their own Duration: or Padding: line are left exactly as written. Long videos (3, 5 and 10 minutes) Pick 3 min, 5 min or 10 min in How long? (Make new video) or Length (the Storyboard). The Smart writer first plans the video as parts, then writes one part at a time: 3 to 10 parts of about 13 scenes, each with a title. The window shows "Writing part 3 of 6..."; Cancel keeps the parts already written. A 10 minute script took about 70 seconds on a desktop with an RTX 4060. Each part starts with a Chapter: line in the script: Visual: coffee farm hills Voice: Coffee grows best on steep, rainy hillsides near the equator. Chapter: Where coffee grows - Storyboard: each chapter is a heading that folds open and shut (only the open one's scenes are shown, so 140 scenes stay quick), and the timeline names the chapters. - In the video: each chapter's title is shown as a card on its first scene. - Upload text: with three or more chapters, their times (0:00 Where coffee grows) are added under the description, which YouTube turns into chapters. They are also saved as name.chapters.txt beside the video. A long video is made in parts of 20 scenes that are joined at the end, with the sound mixed once for the whole video, so the music never restarts. Each scene's clip is opened only while it is on screen: a 3 minute video peaked at about 2 GB of memory, a 10 minute one at 3 GB. Making it takes a while: on that desktop a 3 minute video took about 8 minutes and a 10 minute one about 22 minutes (both 1080p, with captions and music). Stock clips are searched 20 scenes ahead, not all at once, so the sites' limits on searches aren't reached. Stopping a render While a video is rendering, the Render button becomes Cancel. The render stops within a second or two and leaves no unfinished file behind. Captions Captions are on by default: the words appear on screen as they are spoken, timed from the voice itself, so they stay in sync without any setup. Change how they look, or turn them off, in the Captions row on the Storyboard. Scenes without a Voice: line have no captions. The .srt file saved next to the video can be uploaded to YouTube as real subtitles (Subtitles → Upload file → With timing). Footage credits Next to each video the app writes .credits.txt, listing the Pexels or Pixabay creator and page for every stock clip used — handy for a YouTube description. Options Shape (aspect ratio), voice, length, captions and the AI picture look are set per video on the Storyboard; the rest are in Settings. | Setting | Choices | |---|---| | Aspect ratio | 9:16 for Shorts / TikTok / Reels, 16:9 for YouTube | | Resolution | 1080p (8000k bitrate) or 720p (5000k) | | Scene padding | 0s, 0.25s (default), 0.5s or 1s of pause after each voice line | | Voice | 20 free neural voices that run on your PC — see Voices below | | Length | Auto (default), or fit to 15 s, 30 s, 60 s, 3 min, 5 min or 10 min — see Video length and Long videos below | | Versions | 1 (default) or 2: the same video twice, with different clips | | Saving | Ask where to save each video (default): a Save window opens for every render, like a browser download. Off: videos go to the default path and are numbered name (2).mp4, name (3).mp4… so none is overwritten | | Captions | On or off. Style: Highlight, One word or Plain. Size: Small, Medium, Large. Highlight: yellow, green, cyan, pink, white or black. Position: Lower, Center or Top | | Background music | On or off, with any track; ducks under the voice automatically | | Theme | Dark or light, with a Mica backdrop on Windows 11 | Output size follows both settings: 9:16 at 1080p is 1080×1920, 16:9 at 720p is 1280×720, and so on. Where things go | | | |---|---| | Settings | %APPDATA%\AIVideoStudio\settings.json | | My videos | %APPDATA%\AIVideoStudio\projects: script, settings, thumbnail and AI pictures of each video (about 1 MB a picture). The videos themselves stay where you saved them | | Free thumbnails | %APPDATA%\AIVideoStudio\thumbnails: one folder each, with the pictures used in it | | Rendered video | Wherever you choose in the Save window; it opens in your Videos folder the first time. An existing video is only replaced if you confirm it | | Footage credits | .credits.txt, next to the video | | Subtitles | .srt, next to the video (when captions are on) | | Thumbnail | .thumbnail.jpg, next to the video | | Title, description, tags | .upload.txt, next to the video | | Your music | Documents\AI Video Studio\Music | | Log file | %APPDATA%\AIVideoStudio\logs\app.log. It stays on your PC | | Search cache | %APPDATA%\AIVideoStudio\cache, kept for 24 hours (Pixabay's terms require it) | | Temporary clips | %TEMP%\AIVideoStudio, deleted after each render | If the video can't be saved If the folder you chose refuses the file, the app does not lose the render. It saves the video to your Videos folder, then Desktop, then Downloads, then a temp folder, and the Log says which one it used. The usual cause on school and work PCs is Windows Controlled folder access (ransomware protection), which blocks unknown programs from writing to Videos, Documents and Desktop, and makes Save windows answer "file not found". Saving to Downloads or another folder works, or an administrator can allow the app under Windows Security → Virus & threat protection → Ransomware protection. Reporting a problem When a render fails, the error window has a Report this button, and Settings → Help & about → Report a problem works at any time. Both open a report you can read and edit before anything happens: the app version, your Windows version, a few settings, the error, and the last lines of the log. API keys, your Windows user name and the spoken lines of your script are removed first. Nothing is sent by the app. Open GitHub issue opens a prefilled issue in your browser for you to submit, and Copy to clipboard lets you paste the report anywhere else. Needs an internet connection Stock footage (Pexels, Pixabay) comes from the network. Your own local: files, the rendering, the voice and the Smart writer are local; the voice and the Smart writer only need the internet once, for their downloads. AI Script Generation Prompt You can use ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini to automatically write scripts formatted specifically for this app. Copy and paste the prompt template below into your AI of choice: --- > Prompt: > > "You are an expert short-form video scriptwriter for TikTok and YouTube Shorts. > > I need a 45-second high-retention script about: [INSERT TOPIC HERE] > > Strict Formatting Rules: > 1. Output ONLY pairs of lines starting with Visual: and Voice:. > 2. Do NOT include scene numbers, timestamps, markdown asterisks, or extra conversational text. > 3. Visual: must contain 2 to 4 simple, searchable stock video keywords that can be found on Pexels (e.g., 'typing on laptop keyboard', 'neon lightning bolt', 'frustrated person at computer'). > 4. Voice: must contain punchy, engaging spoken dialogue (no emojis, no stage directions). > 5. Create 6 to 8 scene pairs (roughly 100-120 words total). > > Example output format: > Visual: slow broken laptop > Voice: Is your computer taking forever to start up? > > Visual: hands typing on keyboard > Voice: Here is a simple setting tweak to fix it in seconds." --- How to use: 1. Replace [INSERT TOPIC HERE] with your video idea (e.g., '3 hidden iPhone camera features' or 'How to clear cache on Windows'). 2. Copy the AI's exact text output. 3. Paste it directly into the Script editor's box (Settings → Advanced) and click Make video! Run from source Needs Python 3.10+. FFmpeg comes from imageio-ffmpeg, so you do not need to install it separately or add it to PATH. bash git clone cd free-ai-video-generator pip install -r requirements.txt python src/aivideostudio.py The Smart writer also needs llama.cpp, the program that runs its model. This fetches the pinned, checksum-verified Windows build into vendor/llama/: bash python packaging/fetchllama.py Without it the app still runs and uses Quick split. Build the installer yourself bash pip install -r requirements.txt -r requirements-build.txt python -m pytest python packaging/makeicon.py python packaging/fetchllama.py python packaging/fetchespeak.py python packaging/fetchbirefnet.py python packaging/fetchlama.py pyinstaller --noconfirm --clean packaging/aivideostudio.spec "%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Inno Setup 6\ISCC.exe" /DMyAppVersion=5.2.0 packaging\installer.iss That is where Inno Setup goes when installed for one user; installed for everyone, it is C:\Program Files (x86)\Inno Setup 6\ISCC.exe. To time renders on your own PC: python -m vidgen.bench --runs 3 from src, or AIVideoStudio.exe --bench in the installed app (the report lands on the Desktop). Releases are built automatically by GitHub Actions when a v tag is pushed. Code signing policy The Windows builds are not code-signed, so Windows shows a SmartScreen warning the first time you run them (see Download for how to get past it and how to check the file's SHA-256 hash). The project has applied to the SignPath Foundation for free open-source code signing; signed builds will follow if it is accepted. - Builds: every release is built from this repository by GitHub Actions (release workflow); nothing is built or uploaded by hand. - Committers, reviewers and approvers: the repository owner, @bodrumundenizi-beep. Privacy This program does not collect or send any personal data. It connects to other systems only to do what you ask of it: Pexels and Pixabay to search for and download stock footage (using your own API keys). The voiceover is made on your PC; only if you turn on Use Microsoft's online voices is your script text sent to Microsoft Edge's online text-to-speech. On startup it also asks GitHub for this project's latest version number, to tell you about updates; that request contains nothing about you, and you can turn it off under Settings → Updates. An update is only downloaded when you press Update now; it comes from this project's GitHub releases and is checked against the SHA-256 published with the release before it is run. Settings and API keys stay on your computer. The Smart writer runs entirely on your computer. Text you paste into New from text is not sent anywhere. The only connection it makes is the one-time download of the model file from Hugging Face. The app keeps a log file on your PC to help with problems. It is never sent anywhere by the app; a problem report quotes from it only when you choose to send one, and you see the text first. Licence MIT — see LICENSE. The released builds redistribute several third-party components under their own licences, including an LGPL library and a GPL FFmpeg binary. See THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md.

description: Tracks the fastest-growing YouTube music videos, renders horizontal and vertical recaps and publishes them to YouTube, Instagram and TikTok
content:
Repository: olidroide/top-video-generator
    Description: Tracks the fastest-growing YouTube music videos, renders horizontal and vertical recaps and publishes them to YouTube, Instagram and TikTok
    Language: Python
    Topics: automation, bollywood, docker, python, terraform, video-generation, youtube

    README:
    top-video-generator Generate automatically a video resume with the most view growing in a weekly/daily basis. Architecture Overview This application fetches daily/weekly top YouTube music videos for a configured region (currently Bollywood/India), stores timeseries data and metadata, generates videos (horizontal and vertical formats), and publishes to YouTube, Instagram, and TikTok. The diagram below is intentionally high-level. Detailed layer boundaries, migration status, and architecture rules are maintained in ARCHITECTURE.md. System Components mermaid flowchart LR classDef edge fill:#334155,stroke:#7DD3FC,stroke-width:2px,color:#F8FAFC classDef application fill:#1D4ED8,stroke:#93C5FD,stroke-width:2px,color:#EFF6FF classDef domain fill:#065F46,stroke:#34D399,stroke-width:3px,color:#ECFDF5 classDef infra fill:#C2410C,stroke:#FDBA74,stroke-width:2px,color:#FFF7ED classDef platform fill:#BE185D,stroke:#F9A8D4,stroke-width:2px,color:#FFF1F2 classDef store fill:#047857,stroke:#6EE7B7,stroke-width:2px,color:#ECFDF5 subgraph Ingestion ["📥 Ingestion"] FETCH(["Fetch Trending
YouTube API ingestion"]):::infra SCORE{{"Rank & Select
Application orchestration"}}:::application end subgraph Media ["🎬 Media Pipeline"] RENDER(["Render Videos
moviepy / ffmpeg" ]):::infra ASSETS["Templates & Assets
fonts, images, overlays"]:::edge end subgraph Delivery ["🚀 Delivery"] PUBLISH(["Publish Jobs
vertical + weekly" ]):::infra WEB["Web Interface
FastAPI + Jinja2 SSR"]:::edge end subgraph Persistence ["💾 Persistence"] TS[("TinyFlux Timeseries")]:::store DB[("TinyDB Metadata")]:::store VID[("Video Assets videos/")]:::store end subgraph Platforms ["🌍 External Platforms"] YT["YouTube"]:::platform IG["Instagram"]:::platform TT["TikTok"]:::platform end CORE(("Canonical Models
Domain + Ports")):::domain FETCH --> SCORE SCORE --> CORE RENDER --> CORE PUBLISH --> CORE WEB -.-> DB WEB -.-> TS FETCH ==> TS FETCH ==> DB SCORE --> RENDER RENDER -.-> ASSETS RENDER ==> VID PUBLISH -.-> VID PUBLISH ==> YT PUBLISH ==> IG PUBLISH ==> TT style Ingestion fill:#E0F2FE,stroke:#0EA5E9,stroke-width:2px,color:#0C4A6E style Media fill:#FEF3C7,stroke:#F59E0B,stroke-width:2px,color:#451A03 style Delivery fill:#D1FAE5,stroke:#10B981,stroke-width:2px,color:#064E3B style Persistence fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#22C55E,stroke-width:2px,color:#14532D style Platforms fill:#FCE7F3,stroke:#EC4899,stroke-width:2px,color:#831843 Scoring note: ranking logic is canonically implemented in src/domain/services/scoringservice.py and orchestrated by application/use-case flows. Fetch-data orchestration lives in src/application/fetchdatausecase.py, and weekly horizontal publish orchestration lives in src/application/publishvideousecase.py; remaining delivery-layer cleanup is concentrated in shared entrypoint wiring and web contract hardening. Key Components 1. Data Ingestion (src/entrypoints/fetchdata.py) - Scheduled daily fetch from YouTube API - Stores video metadata and view counts - Calculates view growth and rankings - Writes to TinyFlux (timeseries) and TinyDB (metadata) 2. Video Processing Pipeline - Downloader (src/infrastructure/video/downloader.py): Uses yt-dlp to fetch source videos - Processing (src/infrastructure/video/compositor.py, src/infrastructure/video/renderer.py): Composites templates, overlays, and transitions - Workers (src/entrypoints/workers/postprocessor.py): ZeroMQ-based parallel processing 3. Publishing Scripts - Daily Vertical (src/entrypoints/publishvertical.py): Top 5 videos, vertical format for Reels/Shorts - Weekly Horizontal (src/entrypoints/publishvideo.py): Top videos, horizontal format for YouTube 4. Platform Clients - YouTube (src/infrastructure/youtube/ytclient.py): OAuth2, video upload, playlist management - TikTok (src/infrastructure/social/tiktokclient.py): OAuth2, video upload with chunked transfer - Instagram (src/infrastructure/social/instagramclient.py): Session-based auth via instagrapi 5. Web Interface (src/web/main.py) - FastAPI + Jinja2 SSR - OAuth callback handlers for all platforms - Video ranking viewer with date navigation - Background task triggers Technology Stack - Backend: Python 3.13, FastAPI, Pydantic - Video: moviepy, yt-dlp, ffmpeg, PIL - Storage: TinyFlux (timeseries CSV), TinyDB (JSON) - Web: Jinja2 templates, HTMX-ready - Deployment: Docker, Docker Compose - Package Management: uv (ultrafast Python package manager) Configuration All configuration is via environment variables with TOPMUSIC prefix: bash Copy .env.example to .env for local runs and Docker Compose. Use .env.local only if you want an optional untracked override on the same machine. Paths in .env and .env.local are resolved from the repository root. Run uv, make, and docker compose commands from the repository root. Core settings TOPMUSICENV=production|development TOPMUSICDAYSBETWEENTOP=7 YouTube API TOPMUSICYTCLIENTSECRETFILE=secrets/ytclientsecret.json TOPMUSICYTSEARCHREGIONCODE=IN TOPMUSICYTSEARCHLANGUAGECODE=hi Platform credentials (see .env.example) Current Architecture Issues 1. Entrypoint Boundary Debt: fetch-data and weekly horizontal publish orchestration are now use-case owned, but selected entrypoints still contain dependency-wiring detail that should continue moving toward reusable factories and thinner delivery shells. 2. Web Delivery Layer Stabilization: route modules are split under src/web/routes/, but route-level contracts and template boundary tests still need hardening. 3. Monolithic Deployment: A single container still handles fetch, processing, publishing, and web delivery via the STEP environment variable. 4. Local Storage Limits: TinyDB and TinyFlux remain a good fit for single-instance deployments, but they still lack native concurrency controls and stronger operational tooling. 5. Process-Local Observability: /health and /metrics exist, but metrics are in-memory and local to a single process, not centralized or Prometheus-compatible. 6. Scoring Consistency: domain scoring service is canonical, but consistency hardening and regression coverage should continue for ranking semantics. Improvements Implemented ✅ Hexagonal Split (src/domain, src/application, src/adapters, src/infrastructure): Core migration out of legacy god files is completed ✅ Fetch Orchestration Extraction (src/application/fetchdatausecase.py): daily fetch orchestration moved out of the fetch entrypoint into the application layer ✅ Weekly Horizontal Publish Extraction (src/application/publishvideousecase.py): weekly orchestration, idempotency checks, and release persistence now run in the application layer ✅ Vertical Publish Fault Isolation (src/application/publishverticalusecase.py): multi-platform publish fan-out now isolates per-publisher exceptions so one failure does not cancel the full batch ✅ Integration Check Contract Hardening (src/application/checkplatformconnectionusecase.py): unexpected checker failures now return consistent IntegrationCheckResult payloads instead of leaking exceptions upward ✅ Async Isolation (src/infrastructure/): Blocking integrations are isolated with asyncio.tothread() ✅ Retry Utilities (src/utils/retry.py): Exponential backoff with jitter for resilient uploads ✅ Health Checks (/health endpoint): Validates ffmpeg, templates, database ✅ Metrics (/metrics endpoint): Tracks fetch/upload/processing counts and errors ✅ CI/CD (.github/workflows/ci.yml): Automated testing, linting, type checking Planned Improvements - [ ] Separate container services for ingest/process/publish - [ ] Implement dead-letter queue for failed uploads - [ ] Add integration tests with mocked external APIs Explicit Non-Goals - Prometheus metrics export is out of scope for this project. Metrics are intentionally process-local because the system runs on a single server. - A message broker is out of scope for this project. Jobs are not distributed across multiple machines, so adding Redis or RabbitMQ would add operational complexity without solving a real problem. - Migrating metadata storage away from TinyDB is not a current project goal. For the current single-server workload, TinyDB and TinyFlux remain an acceptable fit. Near-Term Next Steps - Continue consolidating shared publish dependency wiring into reusable factories so entrypoints remain thin delivery shells. - Tighten web route and template contract tests under src/web/routes/ to make SSR/HTMX fragments safer to change. - Keep improving scheduler resilience with stronger per-job isolation, retries, and explicit partial-failure reporting. Quick Start Prerequisites - Python 3.13 - ffmpeg installed - ImageMagick installed - Docker (optional) Local Development Important: the file paths configured in .env and .env.local are relative to the repository root. Run the commands below from the repository root so paths like secrets/..., db/..., logs/..., and src/resources/... resolve correctly. bash Install dependencies and git hooks make dev-install make install-hooks Run web server uv run api-server Run data fetch uv run fetch-data Run daily publish uv run publish-vertical Run weekly publish uv run publish-video Dry-run legacy db migration (no writes) uv run migrate-legacy-data Apply legacy db migration (creates source backup) uv run migrate-legacy-data --apply Run quality checks make quality Run the full pre-push gate manually make pre-push-check Optional TikTok Support TikTok publishing now depends on the optional tiktok extra. Use the default install if you do not need TikTok publishing: bash uv sync --all-groups Install the TikTok extra only when you want TikTok integration enabled: bash uv sync --all-groups --extra tiktok TikTok uploader runtime also requires Playwright browser binaries: bash uv run playwright install Git Hooks This repository uses pre-commit as the single hook runner for both commit and push checks. Run this once per clone: bash make install-hooks What happens after that: - git commit runs the pre-commit stage with fast checks for merge conflicts, private keys, whitespace cleanup, ruff check --fix, and ruff format. - git push runs the pre-push stage with the full repository gate: make quality plus pytest tests/ -x -q --ignore=tests/integration/video. Important: a commit can pass and a push can still fail. This is expected because pre-push runs stricter checks (including ty check through make quality) that are not part of the fast pre-commit stage. Useful manual commands: bash Run all pre-commit hooks across the repository make pre-commit-run Run the same checks used by the pre-push hook make pre-push-check If this clone used the older tracked .githooks/ setup before, rerun make install-hooks to migrate to the native .git/hooks installation managed by pre-commit. Start PostgreSQL (if using Docker) docker run -d -p 5432:5432 -e POSTGRESPASSWORD=postgres postgres:16 Development bash Start the Next.js dev server npm run dev Start the video worker (separate terminal) npm run worker Open Prisma Studio to browse data npm run db:studio Open Project Structure src/ app/ # Next.js App Router pages dashboard/page.tsx # Job list dashboard jobs/new/page.tsx # Create job form jobs/[id]/page.tsx # Job detail (logs, artifacts) api/trpc/[trpc]/route.ts # tRPC HTTP handler server/ api/ trpc.ts # tRPC init root.ts # Root router routers/job.ts # Job CRUD router db/index.ts # Prisma client llm/ client.ts # LLM client wrapper schemas.ts # Zod schemas for LLM outputs queue/ index.ts # BullMQ queue setup pipeline.ts # Video generation pipeline remotion/ spec-generator.ts # Remotion project generator tools/ registry.ts # Tool registry (LLM-facing tools) search-images.ts # Image search (SerpAPI) download-image.ts # Image downloader workers/ videoWorker.ts # BullMQ worker entry point lib/ trpc/ client.ts # tRPC React client Provider.tsx # tRPC provider wrapper Pipeline Stages 1. A non-standard value breaks next build during static prerender (useContext / useState null errors). - The npm run build script forces NODEENV=production for next build, but your dashboard env should still be production at runtime. - Optional: use render.yaml in this repo as a blueprint. description: Automated daily YouTube video generation pipeline
content:
Repository: aericheng/youtube-generator
    Description: Automated daily YouTube video generation pipeline
    Language: Python
    Topics: automation, ffmpeg, pipeline, python, video-generation, youtube

    README:
    youtube generator — ambient lofi shorts pipeline Automated daily production of ambient lofi YouTube shorts (Wan 2.2 T2V video + Stable Audio Open music/ambience), fully local on one RTX 5070 Ti. Daily chain LofiShortsDaily (Windows Task Scheduler, 07:00) → rundailyhidden.vbs → rundaily.cmd → pipeline/producedaily.py (topic pick → master clip → slow-motion → music + ambience mix → loop assembly → QC → queue) → pipeline/uploadqueue.py (1 per run; 2 when more than 3 videos are waiting) Output lands in output/queue/ - / (final mp4 + metadata.json). Logs: output/queue/scheduler.log (full run output), output/queue/production.log (one line per day: OK or SKIPPED, with the engine). Master clip engines A14B is first, Wan 5B is the fallback (makemaster in producedaily.py): 1. generatevideoa14b.py: Wan 2.2 T2V A14B GGUF Q4KM, 480x832, 81 frames at 16 fps, about 57 min. 2. upscaleclip.py: center crop to 9:16, Real-ESRGAN general x4v3 at denoise 0.5, 1080x1920. 3. qcpeople.py: RT-DETR person check. Exit 3 means a person was found. A person triggers one retry on a new seed. A second person, a crash, a timeout or no slot for a retry falls back to Wan 5B, which goes through the same person check. If that also shows a person the day is skipped (SKIPPED person in picture). The person check misses blurred, very dark or small people. The retry and 5B pass the idle gate again, and must also start before their deadlines: IDLEDEADLINE (19:40) for a retry, FALLBACKDEADLINE (20:10) for 5B. These only apply before RESERVEDAT (21:30), so a manual rerun later that night works. While the machine is busy each one waits up to its own deadline. No slot for 5B skips the day (SKIPPED gpu busy). Weights live in models/ (not in git): models/a14b/ comes from QuantStack/Wan2.2-T2V-A14B-GGUF and Wan-AI/Wan2.2-T2V-A14B-Diffusers, models/upscale/ from the Real-ESRGAN v0.2.5.0 release. The venv also needs gguf==0.19.0. Tests: python tests/testenginefallback.py. Upload channel gate uploadqueue.py only uploads when the OAuth token acts as exactly the channel in uploadchannelid (pipeline/pool/config.json), so re-authorizing on the wrong account cannot publish to it. Empty id: uploads pause, production keeps running, and videos wait in the queue (exit 0, no alert). Id set, videos waiting, and the token missing or on another channel: nothing uploads and the run exits 1, which raises the failure alert. After a pause the backlog drains at the normal rate: 2 videos per run while more than 3 are waiting, otherwise 1. To switch channels: run .venv\Scripts\python.exe pipeline\ytauth.py, pick the target account, check the channel it prints, then put that id in uploadchannelid. The old token stays in secrets/ as token.json.bak- . Tests: python tests/testuploadguard.py. GPU guard & watchdog Added after the 2026-07-23 incident: the 03:30 run collided with a game left running overnight — denoise ground at 109 s/it (normal 20), crashed after step 1/35, and the leftover contention dragged the whole machine down for hours. - Runs last (idle gate) — added 2026-10-21 after the 07:00 run started next to an RL training run and a 6-worker validation job (VRAM full, RAM into compression). Before any GPU step producedaily.py waits until the whole machine is idle: free VRAM ≥ GPUNEEDMB (14000 MiB), no other python process holding ≥ OTHERGPUMB (256 MiB) of VRAM (read from the Windows GPU Process Memory counter), available RAM ≥ RAMFREEGB (24), CPU over a 60 s sample < CPUBUSYPCT (30 %). It never starts inside NOSTART (10:40–13:00, lab-slack-watch's 12:30 meeting ASR). Busy → re-check every IDLECHECKMIN (15) minutes; no idle slot by IDLEDEADLINE (19:40) → skip the day: writes SKIPPED gpu busy to production.log, the reason to data/last-failure-reason.txt, and exits 2. The process sets itself to idle CPU priority (children inherit it), and the LofiShortsDaily task runs at priority 10 with a 16 h limit to cover the wait. Tests: python tests/testidlegate.py. The gate only decides when to start: a heavy job launched mid-run still competes with it until the step watchdog below. - Step watchdog — every external step goes through run() with a hard timeout: STEPTIMEOUTMIN (30 min) default, A14BTIMEOUTMIN (90 min) for A14B, GENTIMEOUTMIN (60 min) for Wan 5B; a normal full run is 70 min total. On timeout the whole process tree is killed (taskkill /F /T) so nothing can hold RAM/VRAM indefinitely. All knobs are constants at the top of pipeline/producedaily.py. Re-running a skipped or failed day producedaily.py is resumable: run .venv\Scripts\python.exe pipeline\producedaily.py again the same day and it continues from whatever artifacts already exist in the day's folder. A partial folder can never upload: uploadqueue.py only picks folders that have both metadata.json and the final mp4. Weekly report LofiWeeklyReport (Task Scheduler, Mondays 08:40) → runweeklyhidden.vbs → runweekly.cmd → scripts/weeklyreport.py posts one Discord message (same webhook as the daily failure alerts) with four blocks: views and watch time of the last 7 days (Analytics API reports.query, window = today-7 .. yesterday), subscribers gained/lost, top 3 videos by views (titles via Data API videos.list), and the run-log success rate (today-7 .. today from output/queue/scheduler.log: scheduled runs, exitcode 0, produce OK, videos uploaded). On success it writes data/last-success-weekly; on failure runweekly.cmd raises a weekly alert through dailystatus.py. Output of the task: output/queue/weekly.log. First time: authorize once by hand. The token needs the yt-analytics.readonly and youtube.readonly scopes (both are listed in pipeline/ytauth.py). If secrets/token.json was issued without them, the report exits 2 and tells you to re-run the consent: .venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts\weeklyreport.py --auth (equivalent to pipeline/ytauth.py; a browser opens, pick the channel account, then "Advanced" → continue, allow all scopes; token is rewritten to secrets/token.json). Dry run (prints the report and writes data/weekly-report- .md, posts nothing): .venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts\weeklyreport.py --dry-run # real Analytics data .venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts\weeklyreport.py --dry-run --mock # fixture views/subs, real run log --mock is refused without --dry-run, so fixture data never reaches Discord. Register the task (after authorizing): powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\register-weekly.ps1.

description: Automatically generate YouTube Shorts videos with AI-powered scripts for list creation, image generation, audio narration, and video assembly.
content:
Repository: 123filip123/auto-youtube-generator
    Description: Automatically generate YouTube Shorts videos with AI-powered scripts for list creation, image generation, audio narration, and video assembly.
    Language: Python
    Topics: ai, automation, content-creation, gpt-4, image-generation, openai, openai-api, python, text-to-speech, video-generation, youtube

    README:
    Auto YouTube Generator Overview This project automatically generates YouTube Shorts-style videos based on a topic you provide. It uses OpenAI APIs to generate a list of items, create images and audio, and then assembles them into a vertical video suitable for YouTube Shorts. Pipeline steps: 1. Generate a validated list of items (titles, descriptions, image prompts) via JSON-schema structured outputs. 2. Generate every image and voiceover in parallel, capped at MAXCONCURRENTREQUESTS concurrent API calls. 3. Verify every narration exists before continuing. Images may be missing; see When an image fails. 4. Compose each image onto a blurred 1080x1920 backdrop with its title. 5. Assemble the titled images and narration into a vertical video with a slow zoom on each image. 6. Archive the run — list, audio, images, titled images and the finished video — into generateddata/ /. When an image fails OpenAI's safety system sometimes rejects an image, often because the prompt describes a real artwork, album cover or person closely enough to recreate it. The pipeline handles that in two steps: 1. One rewrite. When the image API answers moderationblocked, the text model rewrites that prompt to keep its subject and drop the likely cause, and the image is requested once more. A second rejection fails that image. The rewritten prompt is used only for that image; the saved item list keeps the original. 2. The video is made anyway. An item plays the images it has, splitting its narration evenly between them. An item with no images at all shows a grey question-mark frame with its title. The log names every item that lost images. A missing narration still stops the run, because the item cannot play without it. --- Installation 1. Clone the repository: bash git clone cd auto-youtube-generator 2. Create a virtual environment (optional but recommended): bash python3 -m venv venv source venv/bin/activate For Windows (also make sure you have Python set up in Path): bash python -m venv venv .\venv\Scripts\Activate 3. Install dependencies: bash pip install --upgrade setuptools wheel (do this for windows if you have issues) pip install -r requirements.txt --- OpenAI API Key Setup This app requires access to the OpenAI API for text, image, and audio generation. You must set your API key as an environment variable. 1. Create a .env file in the project root: env OPENAIAPIKEY=youropenaiapikeyhere 2. Alternatively, export the variable in your shell: bash export OPENAIAPIKEY=youropenaiapikeyhere --- Configuration Every tunable lives in config.py and can be overridden with an environment variable of the same name (see .env.example). The ones worth knowing: | Variable | Default | What it does | |---|---|---| | MAXCONCURRENTREQUESTS | 4 | Parallel OpenAI calls. Lower it if you hit rate limits. | | MAXRETRIES | 5 | Attempts per call before giving up. Rate limits and 5xx are retried with exponential backoff. Other 400 errors are not retried; a blocked image prompt gets one rewrite instead (see When an image fails). | | TEXTMODEL | gpt-4.1-mini | Generates the item list. Must support JSON schema structured outputs. | | TTSMODEL | gpt-4o-mini-tts | Narration. Must support the instructions parameter. | | TTSVOICE | ash | Narration voice. | | IMAGEMODEL | gpt-image-1-mini | Image generation. | | IMAGEQUALITY | medium | low is cheaper and faster; high is slower and costs more. | | VIDEOPRESET | medium | x264 preset. ultrafast renders quicker at a larger file size. | --- How to Run the App Run the Pipeline Interactively: bash python main.py Or non-interactively: bash python main.py --topic "Top 5 Extinct Animals" --items 5 Output lands in outputs/, and a complete copy of the run is archived to generateddata/ /. Run the Web UI The web UI is two processes: the FastAPI backend and the Vite dev server. Terminal 1 — backend (must be started from the repository root): bash uvicorn api.app:app --port 8000 Terminal 2 — frontend: bash cd frontend npm install # first time only npm run dev Open . The dev server proxies /api and /media to the backend, so there is nothing else to configure. The UI can: - start a run and watch it stage by stage, with per-asset success and failure - pause after the item list is generated so you can edit titles, descriptions and image prompts before any images or narration are paid for - override any of the tunables listed under Configuration for a single run, without editing .env - switch a single run to production image models with the Production models checkbox on the New Run page - browse every archived run in generateddata/ with its images, narration and video Production models The defaults are the cheap models, for iterating: gpt-4.1-mini writes the list, gpt-image-1-mini at medium quality draws the images and gpt-4o-mini-tts narrates. Ticking Production models generates that run's images with gpt-image-2 at high quality instead. It is slower and costs more, and it changes image generation only. Anything you type into the per-run override fields still wins, so a production run with IMAGEQUALITY set to low uses gpt-image-2 at low. The preset lives in PRODUCTIONIMAGESETTINGS in config.py. The CLI always uses the defaults; set IMAGEMODEL and IMAGEQUALITY in .env to change them there. Only one run can be active at a time. outputs/ is a single shared workspace with fixed filenames, so starting a second run while one is in flight returns a conflict. Cancelling stops the run at the next stage boundary; work already in flight — an OpenAI batch or a video render — finishes first. Run history lives in memory. Restarting the backend clears it — generateddata/ is the durable record. The backend reads config.py and the rest of the code once, at startup. After changing either, restart it, or run it with uvicorn api.app:app --port 8000 --reload while developing so it restarts on every change. To serve the UI from the backend alone (no Vite process), build it first; the backend serves frontend/dist/ at / when that directory exists: bash cd frontend && npm run build --- Output - Generated data (JSON, images, audio, video) will be saved in the outputs/ and generateddata/ directories. - The final video will be in outputs/videooutput/. - outputs/ holds only the latest run. The image and audio folders are emptied when media generation starts, and the titled-image folder when titled images are rendered, so nothing from an earlier run can stand in for a failed asset or end up in this run's archive. - Two runs on the same topic archive to the same generateddata/ / folder. Files the newer run doesn't overwrite stay there. --- Requirements - Python 3.10+ - OpenAI API key - ffmpeg (required by moviepy; install via brew install ffmpeg on macOS or your OS package manager) --- Notes - Make sure your OpenAI account has access to the models listed under Configuration (text, TTS, and image generation). OpenAI retires models over time; an error like "The model 'gpt-image-1' does not exist" means you need to set a model your account still has. - If you hit rate limits, lower MAXCONCURRENTREQUESTS. Transient failures are already retried automatically with exponential backoff. - For best results, use a topic that is suitable for list-style videos (e.g., "Amazing Space Facts"). Demo Video Watch a sample video generated by this tool: Top 5 Most Delicious Sandwiches --- Development Run the test suite: bash pytest Tests never make network calls — every OpenAI interaction goes through an injected fake client, so the suite passes with OPENAIAPIKEY unset. One end-to-end video render is marked slow and takes 30 seconds. Skip it during quick iteration: bash pytest -m "not slow" Frontend tests: bash cd frontend npm test # vitest npm run build # type-check and build Note that moviepy is pinned to 1.0.3 and requires decorator==4.4.2. Upgrading either will break video assembly.

description: Automated daily news poster and YouTube Shorts video generator using Python.
content:
Repository: Ayushmanpaswan/DailyNewsShortsAutomation
    Description: Automated daily news poster and YouTube Shorts video generator using Python.
    Language: Python
    Topics: 

    README:
    Daily News Shorts Automation (Starter) This project generates a 1080×1920 Hindi news poster, turns it into a 6-second MP4 with optional background music, and includes an optional YouTube upload helper. What works out of the box - postergenerator.py: renders the 5-news layout with HTML/CSS + Playwright/Chromium. This avoids Pillow's missing RAQM support. - makevideo.py: creates a 6-second vertical MP4 with FFmpeg. If the music file is absent, it creates a silent video. - youtubeupload.py: optional upload using YouTube Data API v3 and Google OAuth. Important: data/newsdata.json contains sample placeholders. This starter does not fetch real news automatically yet. Replace the five sample items with verified news, or connect a news provider before enabling daily publishing. YouTube uploads are private by default unless you explicitly choose another privacy setting. Windows setup (PowerShell) 1. Extract the ZIP. 2. Open the extracted DailyNewsShortsAutomation folder in VS Code. 3. Install Python 3.11 or 3.12 (recommended for package compatibility) and make sure python works in Terminal. 4. Create and activate a virtual environment: powershell python -m venv .venv ..venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1 python -m pip install --upgrade pip pip install -r requirements.txt pip install -r requirements.txt 5. Generate the poster: powershell python postergenerator.py Output: output/dailynewsposter.png If Hindi font rendering is incorrect, install a Devanagari font such as Nirmala UI or Noto Sans Devanagari on Windows. The Chromium browser uses installed fonts and supports Hindi shaping. 6. Create a video: - Install FFmpeg and add its bin folder to PATH: - Put music you have rights to use at assets/backgroundmusic.mp3. - Then run: powershell python makevideo.py Output: output/dailynewsshort.mp4 You can supply another audio path: powershell python makevideo.py --music "C:\path\to\licensed-music.mp3" --duration 6 YouTube upload setup (optional) 1. In Google Cloud Console, create/select a project and enable YouTube Data API v3. 2. Configure the OAuth consent screen, then create an OAuth Client ID → Desktop app. 3. Download the OAuth JSON and place it at the project root named clientsecret.json. 4. Run this once in a desktop terminal: powershell python youtubeupload.py --privacy private 5. Complete the browser consent. A token.json file will be created locally. Keep both clientsecret.json and token.json private. Never commit them to GitHub. 6. Review the uploaded private video in YouTube Studio. Only use --privacy public after validating the content and upload behavior. YouTube API projects may be subject to quota and audit restrictions; public upload behavior can depend on Google's current API project status. Do not assume public publishing is enabled until tested. GitHub Actions The workflow in .github/workflows/build-video.yml builds the poster and video on a schedule and uploads them as a downloadable workflow artifact. It does not upload to YouTube automatically yet. That is intentional: first verify the output and add news-source automation and securely configured OAuth secrets. To enable the scheduled build: 1. Push this project to a GitHub repository. 2. In the repository, go to Actions and enable workflows. 3. The workflow runs daily at 03:30 UTC (09:00 India Standard Time) and can also be started manually. 4. Add a music file only if you have the rights to use it; GitHub workflow can use a committed, properly licensed audio file or a securely stored asset. GitHub-hosted runners are temporary, so generated files are attached as workflow artifacts. Suggested next stages 1. Replace sample headlines with real, verified news. 2. Add a trusted news API/RSS source and robust error handling. 3. Run the scheduled build and inspect artifacts. 4. Configure and test YouTube upload privately. 5. Only then automate public uploads. Safety and reliability notes - News should be checked for accuracy and dated. - Use music you own or have a license to use. - Do not put OAuth credentials in source control. - A six-second video is very short for five stories; use concise headlines and consider a longer duration if readability suffers.
